a279.t:
Thursday October 2, 2025
Sweden redirected aid money to projects close to the Somali prime minister, in exchange for a migration deal. Credit: Samuel Skoog/Sveriges Radio
Mogadishu (HOL) — Sweden is facing growing political backlash and a diplomatic rift with Somalia after investigations revealed a secret agreement that tied 100 million kronor ($10 million) in Swedish aid to Somalia’s acceptance of deported Somali nationals.
An investigation by Swedish Radio’s news program Ekot revealed that Sweden’s ambassador in Mogadishu reached an agreement in December 2023 with Somalia’s Prime Minister to redirect 100 million kronor from Sweden’s aid budget into a Somali-Italian development fund. In return, Somalia would take back citizens that Sweden wanted to deport, including individuals convicted of crimes who refused to leave.
The deal triggered a year-long conflict between Swedish agencies and Somali authorities. According to Ekot, Somalia’s government insisted on control over the funds through the prime minister’s office, a move analysts say blurred lines between development support and political patronage.
advertisements
“This (deal) is an example of how the Somali government is trying to secure direct control over more resources,” said Omar Mahmood, a Somalia analyst with the International Crisis Group, in an interview with Swedish Radio.When Sweden’s development agency SIDA objected, citing accountability concerns, tensions escalated. To compromise, Sweden transferred 40 million kronor through the World Bank, but the bank later blocked further payments. As disbursements stalled, Somali authorities suspended deportations, accusing Sweden of breaching the agreement.
The standoff culminated in May, when Somalia expelled Sweden’s aid chief, Anna Saleem Högberg, declaring her persona non grata. Somali officials told Ekot they viewed her as “standing in the way of the money.” Shortly afterward, the Swedish government amended SIDA’s mandate, releasing the remaining 60 million kronor via a UNDP-administered program tied to the Somali prime minister’s office. Deportations then resumed.
Experts and former officials have criticized the arrangement as high-risk.
“The goals are vague and the indicators unclear. It’s hard to know whether any outcomes were achieved,” said Mats Hårsmar, deputy director of Sweden’s Expert Group for Aid Studies (EBA).
“The risk of corruption is obvious to anyone who has worked on these issues,” added Wilo Abdulle Osman, a Somali return migration specialist.
Somalia ranks second to last on Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index, and opposition lawmakers in Stockholm have condemned the deal as irresponsible.
“It is highly reckless to transfer such large sums into funds associated with Somalia’s top leadership given the country’s corruption levels,” said Morgan Johansson of the Social Democrats, who demanded a parliamentary inquiry.
The Center Party and Green Party also denounced the agreement as “corruption and political misdirection.” Center Party foreign policy spokesperson Anna Lasses told SVT the revelations were “deeply alarming.”
Minister for International Development Cooperation Benjamin Dousa, of the Moderate Party, defended the policy, saying development aid can be used to promote migration objectives.
“We expect our agencies to deliver on government policy,” Dousa said. “It is reasonable to use aid as an incentive for countries to take back their citizens.”
SIDA officials, however, told Swedish media they felt political pressure from the government to proceed. The agency declined comment, while UNDP said the project complied with its standard accountability procedures.
Sweden first announced plans to deport Somali nationals under new immigration rules in early 2025, targeting individuals with criminal convictions or failed asylum claims. By mid-2025, Sweden had already deported eight Somali nationals and was preparing to remove at least 15 more as part of its stricter immigration crackdown.
The secret deportation agreement follows other schemes Sweden has launched to reduce its migrant population through financial or policy incentives. In September 2024, the government announced an initiative offering refugees, including Somalis, up to 350,000 Swedish kronor (about $35,000) to voluntarily return to their home countries.
Sweden’s approach is part of a Nordic trend of linking development assistance to migration cooperation. In neighbouring Finland, the government froze its Somalia Country Programme in late 2024 after Mogadishu declined to accept more deported citizens, citing security risks and limited reintegration capacity. The freeze halted new project decisions worth 8–9 million euros annually, though humanitarian assistance and NGO grants were allowed to continue. Public broadcaster Yle reported that Helsinki set an informal target of 100 accepted deportees before reconsidering the freeze.
Ekot said it sought comment from the Somali prime minister’s office but received no response.

a335.t:
Ils ont fait vibrer Lola, animé les grandes festivités et porté haut les valeurs culturelles de leur préfecture dans les rencontres artistiques nationales. Aujourd’hui, les membres de Nimba Succès de Lola, autrefois fleuron musical préfectoral, vivent dans l’oubli. Parmi eux, Noutè Bamba, ancien soliste du groupe, livre un témoignage poignant, mêlant souvenirs glorieux et amertume.
« C’est avec Bèrè Jazz que tout a commencé, à Gama Bèrèma, à 42 kilomètres à l’est de la commune urbaine. C’est là que j’ai appris à jouer de la guitare, auprès de Koui Bamba, lui-même formé par feu Aboubacar Demba Camara », se remémore-t-il.
Originaire de Gama Bèrèma, Noutè Bamba arrive à Lola en 1975, lors de la quinzaine artistique nationale. Son premier passage passe inaperçu. Mais en 1978, à l’occasion de la deuxième édition — alors que Lola est érigée en préfecture — il est repéré et intégré au groupe Nimba Succès en tant qu’aide-soliste. Il s’installe alors définitivement dans la ville.
Une vie entièrement dédiée à la musique
Noutè Bamba n’a jamais été à l’école. « Mon père ne m’a pas envoyé à l’école. Moi, c’est la musique que j’aimais », confie-t-il. C’est à l’orchestre qu’il a consacré toute sa vie. En parallèle de ses activités musicales, il travaille dans une scierie, où il gravit les échelons jusqu’à devenir chef des scieurs, puis président préfectoral de la corporation.
« Tout ce que je gagnais, je le mettais dans Nimba Succès. Même les instruments que le groupe utilise encore aujourd’hui, c’est moi qui les ai achetés », affirme-t-il avec fierté.
Grâce à un ami résidant à Yamoussoukro, en Côte d’Ivoire, il parvient à doter l’orchestre de ses premiers équipements modernes. Sous le régime du président Ahmed Sékou Touré, Nimba Succès participe à de nombreux festivals culturels, représentant avec fierté la préfecture de Lola.
Silence et oubli
Mais cette époque est désormais révolue. Aujourd’hui, les artistes du groupe vivent dans l’indifférence générale, privés de reconnaissance et de soutien, malgré leur apport incontestable à la culture nationale.
« Même malades, personne ne vient nous voir. Pourtant, nous avons tout donné pour faire rayonner Lola et la Guinée à travers la musique », déplore Noutè Bamba.
Un cri du cœur pour la reconnaissance
À travers son récit, l’ancien soliste lance un appel pressant aux autorités, aux responsables culturels, aux collectivités locales et à la société civile : « la musique nous a unis. Aujourd’hui, nous demandons simplement à ne pas être oubliés. »
L’histoire de Nimba Succès est celle d’une génération d’artistes passionnés, qui ont fait briller la culture guinéenne sans jamais rien attendre en retour. Ils méritent aujourd’hui une reconnaissance officielle, un minimum de protection sociale et surtout une place dans l’histoire culturelle de la nation.
Car, comme le dit si bien Noutè Bamba : « c’est la musique qui m’a fait connaître. C’est elle qui a tout donné à Lola. »
a335.en:
They made Lola vibrate, enlivened the great festivities and carried high the cultural values of their prefecture at national artistic gatherings. Today, the members of Nimba Succès de Lola, once the prefecture's musical jewel, live in oblivion. Among them, Noutè Bamba, a former soloist of the group, gives a poignant testimony, mixing glorious memories and bitterness.
"It all began with Bèrè Jazz, at Gama Bèrèma, 42 kilometres east of the urban commune. That is where I learned to play the guitar, with Koui Bamba, who was himself trained by the late Aboubacar Demba Camara," he recalls.
Originally from Gama Bèrèma, Noutè Bamba arrived in Lola in 1975, during the national artistic fortnight. His first appearance went unnoticed. But in 1978, on the occasion of the second edition - when Lola was made a prefecture - he was spotted and brought into the group Nimba Succès as an assistant soloist. He then settled permanently in the town.
A life entirely dedicated to music
Noutè Bamba never went to school. "My father did not send me to school. For me, it was music that I loved," he confides. It was to the orchestra that he devoted his whole life. Alongside his musical activities, he worked in a sawmill, where he rose through the ranks to become head of the sawyers, then prefectural president of the trade association.
"Everything I earned, I put into Nimba Succès. Even the instruments the group still uses today, it was I who bought them," he states with pride.
Thanks to a friend living in Yamoussoukro, in Côte d'Ivoire, he managed to provide the orchestra with its first modern equipment. Under the regime of President Ahmed Sékou Touré, Nimba Succès took part in numerous cultural festivals, proudly representing the prefecture of Lola.
Silence and oblivion
But that era is now over. Today, the group's artists live in general indifference, deprived of recognition and support, despite their undeniable contribution to national culture.
"Even when we are sick, no one comes to see us. And yet, we gave everything to make Lola and Guinea shine through music," laments Noutè Bamba.
A heartfelt cry for recognition
Through his account, the former soloist launches a pressing appeal to the authorities, to cultural officials, to local authorities and to civil society: "music united us. Today, we simply ask not to be forgotten."
The story of Nimba Succès is that of a generation of passionate artists who made Guinean culture shine without ever expecting anything in return. Today they deserve official recognition, a minimum of social protection and above all a place in the cultural history of the nation.
For, as Noutè Bamba puts it so well: "it is music that made me known. It is music that gave everything to Lola."

a339.t:
The Landless People's Movement (LPM) is dissatisfied with the level and progression of decentralisation in Namibia.
The party claims that the Ministry of Urban and Rural Development, which is responsible for the decentralisation function, is delaying the transfer of power to local authorities and regional councils.
The political party held a media briefing at Gobabis, where the Africa Decentralisation Day was celebrated.
LPM Councillor Ivan Skrywer said the government must empower local authorities to drive development and build lasting resilience against the challenges facing citizens.
Skrywer noted that while there has been a lot of talk in public forums, there hasn't been much action on the ground.
He also expressed dissatisfaction with the proposed amendments to the Regional Councils Act, which govern the appointment of Chief Regional Officers.
"He stated that appointments now require prior written approval from the minister based on recommendations from the PSC, as the president may resolve disputes. Now, all of a sudden, consultation with the minister is replaced with prior written approval, totally taking away the power of elected officials. Who, by the way, are paying these officials?" Skrywer asked, further stating that "You can't appoint somebody that you're not paying; that is the order of the day, and it should be the order of the day, and that is not the case with the current proposed amendments."
In her speech during the Decentralisation Day, Deputy Minister Evelyn Nawases-Taeyele stated that the government worked towards empowering Regional Councils and Local Authorities through legislative reforms and reviews, capacity building and fiscal resources. But Nawases-Taeyele said there is still a need to enhance the capacity of local institutions to manage resources effectively and transparently.

a568.t:
NEW YORK-(MaraviPost)-President Lazarus Chakwera has left the USA after attending the 79th session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
President Chakwera departed for Malawi through Dulles International Airport on Thursday, October 3.
Account to Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ communication Chakwera will be home on, Saturday, October 5, 2024.
The plane carrying the President is expected to land
at Kamuzu International Airport (KIA) in the capital Lilongwe at 15:45 hours.
While in New York, the President attended several meetings that included, the Summit of the Future and the high-level meeting on the Miombo Forest Declaration ahead of the General Assembly debate.
In his address during the General Assembly debate, the Malawi leader presented a case for UN Security Council reform, lobbying for not only inclusion of Africa in the Council but also veto powers. He also mobilised global support for Malawi’s developmental priorities.
The Malawi leader while in USA also held bilateral discussions with other heads of states and governments of Lativia, Ireland, and Kenya among others.
Chakwera also had special meetings with leaders of International organisations such as the UN Secretary General, Antonio Gutteres and investors among others, to continue advancing Malawi’s diplomatic relations and economic partnerships.
Accompanied by his Mozambican counterpart, Dr. Fillipe J. Nyusi, the Malawi leader also hosted the second Malawi Partners Conference 2024 which brought together prominent global figures and investors who discussed the future and long lasting food security issues.
The conference was attended by, among others, African Development Bank (AFDB) president, Akinwumi Adesina, who announced the grant of MK95 billion to Malawi of which MK1 billion is meant for the purchase of food for people affected by hunger through the Department of Disaster Management Affairs.
After the general debate of the Assembly, the President met up with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Bank and USAID heads at their respective headquarters where he lobbied for their continued support towards Malawi.
The 79th session of UNGA was being held under the theme: Leaving no one behind: Acting together for the advancement of peace, sustainable development and human dignity for present and future generations.

a671.t:
MONROVIA – The ago old saying which speaks to giving someone their flower or due recognition when they are alive became manifest on Thursday, February 6, 2024, when the Minister of Information, Culture and Tourism, Jerolinmek Piah showered praises on Madam Juli Endee, former Cultural Ambassador of the Republic of Liberia, for her immense contributions to the upliftment of Liberia’s cultural heritage.
Making remarks at the auspicious occasion which showcased an array of cultural displays marked by traditional dances, folk singing and renditions of the country’s rich cultural history, Minister Piah said the unveiling of the Arts and Culture Gallery signified the re-opening of the forgotten Cultural Promotion Chapter within the Ministry of Information, Cultural Affairs and Tourism, noting that such feat would not have been achieved without the immense contributions of former Culture Ambassador Juli Endee.
“The unveiling of the rich Liberian arts and culture gallery is one the first steps towards the promotion of our cultural heritage. Cultural Promotion was given serious attention at MICAT from 1951 to 1990. Adequate budgetary support was given to the National Cultural Center and Troupe, a well-stocked National Museum and vibrant Tubman Center for Arts and Culture in Robertsports. The war and post war eras neglect seriously affected this important responsibility of MICAT.
“Since the ascendency of me and my team in 2024, we continue to maintain and direct equal focus not only on government information dissemination, but also tourism development and cultural heritage promotion.
“Throughout the years and before today when one entered MICAT, there was visibly nothing to indicate that MICAT is also the sector lead for cultural promotion.
“For this reason and with an excellent concept and breath-taking creativity of former Cultural Ambassador Queen Juli Endee, we embarked upon and now see this impressive display of our Liberia’s rich cultural artefacts,” Minister Piah said.
Continuing, Minister Piah said the gallery gives one the feeling about how diverse and rich Liberia’s cultural heritage is. MICAT is not only stopping here; We will ensure the reactivation of the National Cultural Center; reorient the National Cultural Troupe with the help of our county leaderships to recruit new talents across the country to replace those who have advanced in age.
“Already, MICAT has pitched to UNESCO Headquarters in Paris through inter-ministerial collaboration with the Ministry of Education, the revamping, restocking and repositioning of our National Museum where students and the public will visit to learn more about the country’s cultural heritage.
“These are the tasks we are embarking upon and with full and adequate support, the lost glory of this entity can and will be restored. As you can see, the process of completely re-making MICAT is well on course – New roof that will last for decades, refurbished offices, reconditioned walls and ceilings, improved electrical system etc.
“Phase II will see the replacements of windows, doors, ceiling, reconditioning/building of restrooms, offices, floors, the fence, landscaping among others. Together, we can think, love and build our cultural diversities and richness to foster national unity and economic prosperity,” Minister Piah said.
Former Cultural Ambassador Juli Endee for her part praised authorities at the Ministry of Information for always providing the platform for her involvement in promoting the country’s rich arts and culture heritage.
“It’s always a pleasure to be here at the Ministry of Information, Cultural Affairs and Tourism. I’ve worked with past and present leaders of this Ministry.
“As a traditional queen of the republic of Liberia, I am leaving within this Ministry very important artifacts of arts, culture and tourism. Creativity and imagination equal innovation. So, today we are here to unveil a dream. I want to thank my father Joseph Nyuma Boakai, Sr., who has given me the opportunity to serve as Commissioner General of the World Expo in Japan. I am also on the International World Expo Committee for Exhibition, and I will be taking Liberia to Japan,” Ambassador Endee said.
Speaking in his capacity as Liberia’s new Cultural Ambassador, Mr. Kekura Kamara promised to use his platform to bring the government to the people. He used the occasion to inform of a new cultural roadshow planned for the first week in every February where Liberian culture will be displayed and the ARREST Agenda showcased through cultural performances. The Western Region Culture Show held recently in Besao is the precursor to this national cultural event.
Special Presidential Envoy on Tourism Ambassador Christopher Onanuga also used the occasion to express elation for being part of such a unique occasion.
“I am overjoyed because tourism is the embodiment of growth in every sector of the economy in every nation. And when we pursue it, it shines the light. Ninety percent of tourists come to Africa. This time around for the next 200 years they will be coming only because of heritage purposes,” Ambassador Onanuga said.
Speaking further, President Boakai’s special tourism envoy underscored the importance of the media in promoting tourism and called on the Fourth Estate to put up the plate for his national duty call.
“The Fourth Estate has a critical role to play in selling tourism. Talk about it, let everybody know what’s going on. When you look at the newspapers, the online TV, the websites, the TV, nothing is dedicated to tourism, the arts and culture,” he said.
As for Representative Bernard Blue Benson who also Chairs the House Committee on Information, Broadcasting Culture and Tourism, tourism cannot strive without an organized and functioning culture.
“We support the reestablishment of Kendeja. If we are serious about tourism, the re-establishment of Kendeja must be prioritized. Kendeja serves as our cultural identity. Mr. Vice President, Senator Dillon, all members of this high table, we must put our hands together to reestablish Kendeja. If you are to be serious to boost Liberia to the world, the engine that serves as our cultural identity that has been destroyed must be reestablished,” Representative Benson said.
Also making remarks, the Senate Chairman on Information, Broadcasting, Culture and Tourism, Senator Abraham Darius Dillon said the Liberian Senate in recent times concurred with the House of Representatives to pass into law the Tourism Act to give autonomy to the tourism industry.
“As we speak the endorsed bill is on its way to the Executive Mansion for approval and printing into handbill. We did that on purpose because it is a legacy agenda of the Joseph Nyuma Boakai administration. We go to other countries; we see their tourism sectors booming. They are booming not because of magic but because deliberate concrete steps are taken towards achieving this goal.
“Creation of the Tourism Commission is not sufficient. We must fund it. We will do everything to ensure there is budgetary support. We look forward to the Executive considering the latest action of the United States government when it comes to USAID,” Senator Dillon said, while calling on all government ministries and agencies to use the Liberia Broadcasting System to break all government news.
Making remarks, Dr. Augustine Konneh, Advisor to the President, said the unveiling of the arts and culture galleries is a true manifestation of Liberian culture, its inheritance, and heritage. “If you do not write about your own culture, your history; someone will write it for you. And if they write it for you, you will not like it,” Dr. Konneh said.
Commenting also, Justice Minister Oswald Tweh said the occasion was a milestone that all Liberians must be proud of. “Our cultural heritage is very important. When people come to your country, they don’t come to see what they have, but what they don’t have,” Cllr. Tweh said.
VP Koung Underlines importance of arts and culture
Climaxing and launching the Arts and Culture Gallery at MICAT, Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung emphasized the importance of cultural preservation and tourism.
VP Koung used the occasion to reaffirm the significance of preserving Liberia’s cultural heritage, characterizing it as a foundational pillar of the nation’s identity and development, noting, “culture cannot be overlooked” and called for concerted efforts to safeguard and promote Liberia’s cultural traditions.
Vice President Koung specifically noted the necessity of enhancing Liberian colloquialisms and integrating them into the national education system.
VP Koung also spoke glowingly on the issue of tourism, urging the government to prioritize investments in the tourism sector. He especially called for the restoration of the iconic yet neglected Hotel Africa, observing that its revitalization could serve as a symbol of Liberia’s tourism potential and generate significant revenue for the country.
While commending the Minister of Information, Cultural Affairs, and Tourism for conceptualizing the Arts and Culture Galleries, Vice President Koung also expressed gratitude to the legislature for the recent passage of the Tourism Bill, which facilitates the establishment of the National Tourism Commission.
Speaking further, Vice President Koung underscored the importance of investing in media, highlighting that effective information dissemination is vital to the nation’s progress, stating, “Information dissemination remains crucial to the development process”.
He then called for enhanced government support to strengthen media infrastructure and its role in promoting Liberia’s cultural and economic initiatives.
The event brought together numerous dignitaries, including members of the legislature, cabinet ministers, presidential advisors, and ambassadors, among others. The program was interspersed with eye-feasting cultural performances.

a909.t:
La Nation Bénin...
Après cinq années d’intervention, le Projet des services de
santé intégrés (Ihsa) au Bénin a abouti à des résultats significatifs mis en
lumière, ce mardi 17 octobre à Cotonou, à la faveur d’un atelier de
dissémination qui marque la clôture des activités. Il s’agit d’en prendre de la
graine pour la pérennisation des acquis.
Les parties prenantes du Projet « Integrated Health
Services Activity » (Activité des services de santé intégrés /Ihsa) se
félicitent des résultats probants obtenus en cinq ans de mise en œuvre
(2018-2023) dans les départements de l’Alibori, de l’Atacora, de l’Ouémé et du
Plateau. Un atelier de clôture organisé, ce mardi 17 octobre à Cotonou, a
permis de passer en revue les progrès enregistrés, d’en tirer les enseignements
pour la consolidation des acquis.
D’un montant de 22,5 millions de dollars Us soit environ 13,9 milliards F Cfa financé par l’Agence des Etats-Unis pour le développement international (Usaid), le projet Ihsa visait à renforcer les capacités locales pour offrir des soins de santé de qualité à travers des prestations à fort impact pour le paludisme, la planification familiale, la santé maternelle et infantile et les violences basées sur le genre (Vbg), la prévention et la lutte contre la Covid-19, rappelle Brinille Eliane Ellis, chef de mission adjoint de l’ambassade des Etats-Unis d’Amérique près le Bénin. Il est mis en œuvre par l’organisation internationale Management Sciences for Health (Msh) en partenariat avec Dimagi et quatre partenaires locaux à savoir Cerrhud, Ceradis, Dedras et Apessa, avec un fort engagement du gouvernement et des citoyens.
Le directeur de cabinet du ministre de la Santé se réjouit, au niveau institutionnel, de la mise en place d’une application numérique dénommée « AlafiaComm » pour la gestion des données communautaires. Dr Enagnon Pétas Akogbéto salue également le développement de la première maquette d’une carte sanitaire digitale pour faciliter les prises de décisions, la mise à jour des documents normatives, guides et outils de supervision, le renforcement du système de santé à travers les dons de matériel et équipements nécessaires aux soins obstétricaux et néonataux d’urgence (Sonu), à la prévention et au contrôle de l’infection, grâce au projet.
Plateau technique renforcé
Un appui technique et financier à la première campagne de chimioprophylaxie contre le paludisme a permis de protéger 1,8 million d’enfants de moins de 5 ans entre 2019 et 2022, détaille Dr Floride Niyuhiré, directrice du projet. La fourniture de matériel et d’équipements d’une valeur de 4 milliards F Cfa environ a permis de renforcer le plateau technique des formations sanitaires. Et, avec la survenue de la pandémie de Covid-19, le projet a permis de sensibiliser près de 2 millions de personnes dont plus d’un million ont été vaccinées contre le coronavirus, ajoute-t-elle.
Aux côtés des Centres de promotion sociale (Cps), le projet a accompagné les survivants de Vbg en leur fournissant des soins médicaux, un soutien psychosocial, une prise en charge judiciaire et des opportunités de réinsertion socioprofessionnelle, note Dr Agnès Oladoun Badou Savi, directrice adjointe de cabinet du ministre des Affaires sociales et de la Microfinance (Masm). Elle affirme la volonté du ministère des Affaires sociales de maintenir et de renforcer les acquis, dont l’opérationnalisation du Système informatisé des données sur la famille, la femme et l’enfant – Nouvelle.
Brinille E. Ellis, pour sa part, réitère l’engagement du
gouvernement des Etats-Unis à soutenir les efforts du Bénin dans le secteur de
la santé.
--------------- Appui conséquent aux victimes de violences ---------------------
Outre la réduction de la mortalité maternelle et infantile,
le projet Ihsa a mis un accent particulier sur la lutte contre les violences
basées sur le genre (Vbg). Au total, 687 agents de santé, 140 assistants
sociaux et 302 agents de police judiciaire ont été formés aux procédures standards
pour la prise en charge des survivants de Vbg. 
Entre 2019 et 2022, le nombre de survivants des Vbg pris en
charge est passé de 79 à 652 pour les soins cliniques, de 1 177 à
5 551 pour le soutien psychosocial, et de 179 à 1 623 pour
l’assistance judiciaire.
Dans une approche holistique, 77 % des victimes sont
financièrement indépendantes. En effet, dans trois départements, 229 survivants
ont été formés pour développer des activités génératrices de revenu appuyées
par le projet, en bénéficiant du coaching sur la gestion de fonds,
l’identification des marchés ainsi que d’équipements pour le développement de
leurs activités.
a909.en:
Integrated health services project: Praiseworthy gains to be sustained

La Nation Benin...

After five years of intervention, the Integrated Health Services Project (Ihsa) in Benin has led to significant results highlighted this Tuesday 17 October in Cotonou at a dissemination workshop marking the closure of activities. The point is to learn from them in order to sustain the gains.

The stakeholders of the "Integrated Health Services Activity" (Ihsa) project are pleased with the convincing results obtained over five years of implementation (2018-2023) in the departments of Alibori, Atacora, Ouémé and Plateau. A closing workshop organised this Tuesday 17 October in Cotonou made it possible to review the progress recorded and to draw lessons for the consolidation of the gains.

Worth $22.5 million US, or about 13.9 billion CFA francs, financed by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the Ihsa project aimed to strengthen local capacities to offer quality health care through high-impact services for malaria, family planning, maternal and child health and gender-based violence (GBV), and the prevention of and fight against Covid-19, recalls Brinille Eliane Ellis, Deputy Chief of Mission of the Embassy of the United States of America to Benin. It is implemented by the international organisation Management Sciences for Health (MSH) in partnership with Dimagi and four local partners, namely Cerrhud, Ceradis, Dedras and Apessa, with strong engagement from the government and from citizens.

The Chief of Staff of the Minister of Health is pleased, at the institutional level, with the establishment of a digital application called "AlafiaComm" for the management of community data. Dr Enagnon Pétas Akogbéto also welcomes the development of the first model of a digital health map to facilitate decision-making, the updating of normative documents, guides and supervision tools, and the strengthening of the health system through donations of materials and equipment needed for emergency obstetric and neonatal care (EmONC) and for infection prevention and control, thanks to the project.

Strengthened technical capacity

Technical and financial support for the first malaria chemoprophylaxis campaign made it possible to protect 1.8 million children under the age of 5 between 2019 and 2022, details Dr Floride Niyuhiré, director of the project. The supply of materials and equipment worth about 4 billion CFA francs made it possible to strengthen the technical capacity of health facilities. And, with the onset of the Covid-19 pandemic, the project made it possible to raise awareness among nearly 2 million people, of whom more than a million were vaccinated against the coronavirus, she adds.

Alongside the Social Promotion Centres (CPS), the project supported GBV survivors by providing them with medical care, psychosocial support, judicial assistance and opportunities for socio-professional reintegration, notes Dr Agnès Oladoun Badou Savi, Deputy Chief of Staff of the Minister of Social Affairs and Microfinance (Masm). She affirms the willingness of the Ministry of Social Affairs to maintain and strengthen the gains, including the operationalisation of the Computerised System of Data on the Family, Women and Children – New.

Brinille E. Ellis, for her part, reiterates the commitment of the United States government to support Benin's efforts in the health sector.

--------------- Substantial support for victims of violence ---------------------

In addition to reducing maternal and child mortality, the Ihsa project placed particular emphasis on the fight against gender-based violence (GBV). In total, 687 health workers, 140 social workers and 302 judicial police officers were trained in standard procedures for the care of GBV survivors.

Between 2019 and 2022, the number of GBV survivors cared for rose from 79 to 652 for clinical care, from 1,177 to 5,551 for psychosocial support, and from 179 to 1,623 for judicial assistance.

In a holistic approach, 77% of victims are financially independent. Indeed, in three departments, 229 survivors were trained to develop income-generating activities supported by the project, benefiting from coaching on fund management, market identification, as well as equipment for the development of their activities.

a983.t:
Le Président de la République, Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, à la tête d’une importante délégation, a pris part jeudi au sommet des pays de la ligue Arabe accueilli cette année par le Royaume de Bahreïn. La guerre meurtrière qui ravage depuis plus de sept mois la bande de Gaza a dominé les discussions.
es délégations des 22 pays membres de l’organisation des pays arabes, parmi lesquelles des chefs d’Etat et de gouvernements ainsi que des souverains arabes mais également des dirigeants d’organisations internationales, se sont retrouvés le jeudi 16 mai 2024 au palais ‘‘Al-Sakhir’’, sis à l’Ouest de la capitale Manama, dans le cadre du 33e sommet ordinaire des pays de la ligue arabe qui s’est tenu pour la première fois au Royaume de Bahreïn.
Plusieurs points concernant la paix et la sécurité des peuples arabes dont notamment celles du peuple palestinien étaient à l’ordre de jour de ce nouveau sommet intervenu pour la seconde fois depuis le début des hostilités de la guerre mené par l’armée israélienne à Gaza.
Arrivée le mercredi soir dans la capitale du royaume de Bahreïn où flottent les drapeaux des 22 pays membres de la Ligue arabe, le président de la république, Ismail Omar Guelleh, a dans une importante allocution prononcée au cours de ce sommet, mis en lumière les enjeux cruciaux, tout en exprimant sa gratitude envers les hôtes du sommet, soulignant dans la foulée l’importance de l’action collective dans la région.
« Tout d’abord, je tiens à exprimer mes sincères remerciements et ma profonde appréciation à Sa Majesté le Roi Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, ainsi qu’à son gouvernement et à son peuple, pour leur accueil chaleureux, leur généreuse hospitalité et la préparation remarquable de ce sommet », a d’emblée déclaré le président Ismail Omar Guelleh avant de remercier également Sa Majesté le Roi Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saoud, Serviteur des Deux Saintes Mosquées, ainsi que Son Altesse Royale le prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saoud, Prince Héritier, et le Secrétaire général de la Ligue arabe et son personnel, les uns pour leurs efforts déployés quant à l’organisation du précédent sommet et les autres pour leurs efforts à renforcer l’action arabe commune.
Evoquant par la suite l’agression continue d’Israël contre la bande de Gaza, « exposant au monde entier les crimes les plus horribles contre l’humanité », le Président de la République de Djibouti, également Président en exercice de l’IGAD, a souligné: « Notre réunion survient à un moment critique alors que la région arabe est confrontée à des défis sans précédent. » «Nous reconnaissons la gravité de cette tragédie et appelons à une réponse arabe unie pour mettre fin à cette guerre d’extermination contre notre peuple à Gaza », a appelé le Président Guelleh et d’insister ensuite sur un cessez-le-feu immédiat et durable pour protéger les civils, en vue de mettre « fin aux déplacements forcés et assurer un accès sûr à l’aide humanitaire».
Pour le président djiboutien, « la nécessité de relancer le processus de paix en soutenant la solution à deux États conformément aux résolutions internationales et en reconnaissant la Palestine comme membre à part entière de l’ONU, permettant ainsi au peuple palestinien de réaliser ses droits légitimes et d’établir un État indépendant avec Jérusalem-Est comme capitale » constitue une nécessité absolue pour assurer un avenir sûr et prospère pour tous les peuples de la région.
En ce qui concerne le contexte des crises qui affectent certains pays arabes, la persistance des tensions au Yémen et en Libye, ainsi que la crise prolongée au Soudan, le président de la république, Ismail Omar Guelleh, appelle à « une action collective arabe efficace ». « Si nous ne coopérons pas pour endiguer ces crises, elles risquent de se prolonger avec des conséquences désastreuses pour le Soudan et la région dans son ensemble. La résolution de ces crises exige un effort collectif et urgent, comme je l’ai souligné précédemment », a-t-il précisé avant de mettre l’accent sur « les efforts déployés par la République de Djibouti, notamment dans le cadre de sa présidence tournante de l’IGAD, pour contribuer à la résolution de la crise au Soudan ». « Djibouti réaffirme son accueil et son soutien total à toutes les initiatives visant à aider les Soudanais à surmonter cette épreuve et à trouver une solution politique globale à la crise» pour mettre fin à cette autre guerre dévastatrice, a-t-il
indiqué. Face à l’intensification de la division et de la polarisation à l’échelle internationale, qui ont engendré, selon le président de Djibouti, « une lutte pour l’imposition de volontés divergentes et l’application inégale du droit international », « nous devons nous tourner vers nos propres capacités », a déclaré M. Ismail Omar Guelleh, avant de souligner l’importance « de renforcer notre collaboration et d’unifier nos efforts pour élaborer des solutions décisives et radicales aux défis actuels et futurs qui menacent notre nation». « Cela nécessitera inévitablement le développement et la promotion d’une coopération arabe renouvelée, adoptant une approche novatrice qui met en avant les préoccupations des citoyens arabes au premier plan de nos priorités », a-t-il poursuivi.
Il a également appelé à renforcer la coopération arabe pour faire face aux défis actuels et futurs, en mettant l’accent sur les besoins des citoyens arabes et en adoptant une approche novatrice pour élaborer des solutions décisives.
Enfin, le président Guelleh a exprimé son soutien à la candidature de Mahmoud Ali Youssouf à la présidence de la Commission de l’Union africaine, soulignant ainsi l’importance de l’unité africaine dans la poursuite du développement et de la prospérité du continent. En conclusion, le président Guelleh a adressé ses sincères remerciements à l’hôte du sommet, le Royaume de Bahreïn, pour son accueil et sa préparation exemplaire, et a invoqué la guidance divine pour le succès des nations et des peuples arabes. Ce discours illustre l’engagement du président Guelleh envers la paix, la stabilité et le développement dans la région arabe, ainsi que sa vision d’une action collective et coopérative pour relever les défis communs auxquels sont confrontés les pays arabes.
Des rencontres en marge
En marge du 33e sommet ordinaire de la Ligue des États arabes à Manama
(Bahreïn), le président djiboutien, Ismail Omar Guelleh, a tenu des réunions essentielles avec les présidents égyptien Abdel Fattah al-Sissi, le libyen Mohammed al-Manfi et le mauritanien Mohamed Ould Ghazouani.
Lors de ces échanges bilatéraux, le président Guelleh a souligné l’importance de la coopération régionale pour faire face aux défis sécuritaires et humanitaires qui touchent la Libye et la région dans son ensemble. Les discussions ont également porté sur les opportunités de collaboration en vue de promouvoir la paix, la sécurité et la reconstruction dans des contextes fragiles.
La rencontre avec le président égyptien Al-Sissi a permis d’aborder des enjeux majeurs tels que les questions sécuritaires régionales, en mettant l’accent sur la situation en Palestine. Les deux dirigeants ont exploré des moyens de renforcer les liens stratégiques entre Djibouti et l’Égypte, notamment dans des domaines clés tels que la sécurité, l’économie et la diplomatie.
Quant à la réunion avec le président libyen Al-Manfi, le président Guelleh a exprimé un soutien ferme au processus de transition en Libye, soulignant la nécessité cruciale d’instaurer une stabilité durable pour le bien-être du pays et de la région. Les discussions ont mis en lumière les défis sécuritaires et humanitaires auxquels la Libye est confrontée, tout en explorant les voies possibles pour une coopération régionale plus étroite afin de relever ces défis de manière effective.
Ces rencontres importantes illustrent l’engagement continu du président Guelleh en faveur de la promotion de la coopération et de la stabilité régionales au sein du monde arabe. Elles offrent également une plate-forme essentielle aux dirigeants arabes pour partager leurs perspectives, coordonner leurs efforts et renforcer leur solidarité face aux défis régionaux complexes et en évolution constante.
Avec le président mauritanien, il a abordé des questions sécuritaires et économiques régionales, avec des discussions approfondies sur la situation en Palestine et l’importance de renforcer la coopération bilatérale.
Ces échanges reflètent l’engagement du président Guelleh en faveur de la coopération et de la stabilité régionale, enrichissant ainsi les dialogues du sommet de la Ligue des États arabes. La délégation djiboutienne, dirigée par le président Guelleh et composée du ministre des Affaires Étrangères et de la coopération internationale, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, et nos ambassadeurs en Arabie Saoudite et en Egypte, respectivement Dya Eddine Bamakhrama et Ahmed Ali Barreh, démontre l’importance que la république de Djibouti accorde à ces discussions de haut niveau.
En effet, le 33e sommet des pays membres de la Ligue Arabe est survenu à un moment où la République de Djibouti est en lice pour la présidence de la commission de l’Union Africaine.
Déclaration de Bahreïn Les dirigeants arabes réaffirment leur engagement en faveur de la paix et condamnent l’agression israélienne contre la bande de Gaza
Les dirigeants des États arabes ont adopté une déclaration finale à l’issue du 33e Sommet du Conseil des États arabes à Bahreïn, marquant un engagement renouvelé en faveur de la solidarité et de la prospérité dans la région. Sous la présidence de Sa Majesté le Roi du Royaume de Bahreïn, les chefs d’Etat et de gouvernement ont réaffirmé leurs liens de fraternité et d’histoire commune, soulignant l’importance d’une action collective pour préserver la sécurité et la stabilité des États arabes.
La déclaration met en exergue une vision stratégique commune pour promouvoir la coopération et l’intégration dans tous les domaines, dans l’intérêt des peuples arabes. Les dirigeants ont également exprimé leur engagement en faveur de la paix, de la tolérance et de la coexistence pacifique, tout en condamnant fermement le terrorisme sous toutes ses formes.
Une large partie de la déclaration est consacrée à la question palestinienne, avec une condamnation sans équivoque de l’agression israélienne contre la bande de Gaza et un appel urgent à mettre fin à cette agression, à lever le blocus et à permettre l’entrée d’aide humanitaire. La déclaration a également exprimé un soutien solide à des pays tels que le Soudan, la Syrie, le Yémen et la Libye dans leurs efforts pour assurer la stabilité, la sécurité et la prospérité, tout en appelant à des solutions politiques conformes aux aspirations de leurs peuples.
Enfin, les dirigeants arabes se sont engagés à renforcer les partenariats avec les alliances internationales et à coopérer avec les Nations unies pour relever les défis mondiaux, y compris la réalisation des objectifs de développement durable à l’horizon 2030.
Le Sommet de Bahreïn a été salué comme une étape importante dans la promotion de la solidarité et de la prospérité arabes, illustrant la détermination des pays arabes à surmonter les défis et à œuvrer ensemble pour un avenir meilleur pour la région.La déclaration finale reflète l’engagement profond des États arabes à renforcer leur coopération régionale et à relever les défis communs dans un contexte de bouleversements géopolitiques et de transformations économiques.
a983.en:
33rd Arab League Summit: The deadly war in Gaza dominates the discussions in Manama

The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, at the head of an important delegation, took part on Thursday in the summit of the Arab League countries hosted this year by the Kingdom of Bahrain. The deadly war that has ravaged the Gaza Strip for more than seven months dominated the discussions.

The delegations of the 22 member countries of the organisation of Arab countries, among them heads of state and government as well as Arab sovereigns but also leaders of international organisations, gathered on Thursday 16 May 2024 at the "Al-Sakhir" palace, located west of the capital Manama, as part of the 33rd ordinary summit of the Arab League countries, held for the first time in the Kingdom of Bahrain.

Several points concerning the peace and security of the Arab peoples, notably those of the Palestinian people, were on the agenda of this new summit, which took place for the second time since the outbreak of hostilities in the war waged by the Israeli army in Gaza.

Having arrived on Wednesday evening in the capital of the Kingdom of Bahrain, where the flags of the 22 member countries of the Arab League fly, the President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, in an important address delivered during this summit, highlighted the crucial issues at stake, while expressing his gratitude towards the summit's hosts, underlining at the same time the importance of collective action in the region.

"First of all, I would like to express my sincere thanks and deep appreciation to His Majesty King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa, as well as to his government and his people, for their warm welcome, their generous hospitality and the remarkable preparation of this summit," President Ismail Omar Guelleh declared at the outset, before also thanking His Majesty King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, as well as His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince, and the Secretary General of the Arab League and his staff, the former for their efforts in organising the previous summit and the latter for their efforts to strengthen joint Arab action.

Subsequently evoking Israel's continued aggression against the Gaza Strip, "exposing to the whole world the most horrific crimes against humanity", the President of the Republic of Djibouti, also the current Chairman of IGAD, stressed: "Our meeting comes at a critical moment while the Arab region is confronted with unprecedented challenges." "We recognise the gravity of this tragedy and call for a united Arab response to put an end to this war of extermination against our people in Gaza," President Guelleh urged, and then insisted on an immediate and lasting ceasefire to protect civilians, with a view to putting "an end to forced displacement and ensuring safe access to humanitarian aid".

For the Djiboutian president, "the need to revive the peace process by supporting the two-State solution in accordance with international resolutions and by recognising Palestine as a full member of the UN, thus allowing the Palestinian people to realise their legitimate rights and establish an independent State with East Jerusalem as its capital" constitutes an absolute necessity to ensure a safe and prosperous future for all the peoples of the region.

Regarding the context of the crises affecting certain Arab countries, the persistence of tensions in Yemen and Libya, as well as the prolonged crisis in Sudan, the President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, called for "effective collective Arab action". "If we do not cooperate to contain these crises, they risk being prolonged with disastrous consequences for Sudan and the region as a whole. Resolving these crises requires a collective and urgent effort, as I have stressed previously," he specified, before emphasising "the efforts made by the Republic of Djibouti, notably within the framework of its rotating presidency of IGAD, to contribute to resolving the crisis in Sudan". "Djibouti reaffirms its welcome and its total support for all initiatives aimed at helping the Sudanese overcome this ordeal and find a comprehensive political solution to the crisis," in order to put an end to this other devastating war, he indicated.

Faced with the intensification of division and polarisation at the international level, which have given rise, according to the president of Djibouti, to "a struggle for the imposition of divergent wills and the unequal application of international law", "we must turn to our own capacities," declared Mr Ismail Omar Guelleh, before underlining the importance "of strengthening our collaboration and unifying our efforts to develop decisive and radical solutions to the current and future challenges that threaten our nation". "This will inevitably require the development and promotion of renewed Arab cooperation, adopting an innovative approach that puts the concerns of Arab citizens at the forefront of our priorities," he continued.

He also called for strengthening Arab cooperation to face current and future challenges, emphasising the needs of Arab citizens and adopting an innovative approach to develop decisive solutions.

Finally, President Guelleh expressed his support for the candidacy of Mahmoud Ali Youssouf for the presidency of the African Union Commission, thereby underlining the importance of African unity in the pursuit of the continent's development and prosperity. In conclusion, President Guelleh extended his sincere thanks to the summit's host, the Kingdom of Bahrain, for its welcome and its exemplary preparation, and invoked divine guidance for the success of Arab nations and peoples. This speech illustrates President Guelleh's commitment to peace, stability and development in the Arab region, as well as his vision of collective and cooperative action to meet the common challenges facing Arab countries.

Meetings on the sidelines

On the margins of the 33rd ordinary summit of the League of Arab States in Manama (Bahrain), the Djiboutian president, Ismail Omar Guelleh, held essential meetings with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, Libya's Mohammed al-Manfi and Mauritania's Mohamed Ould Ghazouani.

During these bilateral exchanges, President Guelleh underlined the importance of regional cooperation to address the security and humanitarian challenges affecting Libya and the region as a whole. The discussions also covered opportunities for collaboration with a view to promoting peace, security and reconstruction in fragile contexts.

The meeting with Egyptian President Al-Sisi made it possible to address major issues such as regional security questions, with an emphasis on the situation in Palestine. The two leaders explored ways of strengthening the strategic ties between Djibouti and Egypt, notably in key areas such as security, the economy and diplomacy.

As for the meeting with Libyan President Al-Manfi, President Guelleh expressed firm support for the transition process in Libya, underlining the crucial need to establish lasting stability for the well-being of the country and the region. The discussions highlighted the security and humanitarian challenges facing Libya, while exploring possible avenues for closer regional cooperation to meet these challenges effectively.

These important meetings illustrate President Guelleh's continued commitment to promoting regional cooperation and stability within the Arab world. They also offer an essential platform for Arab leaders to share their perspectives, coordinate their efforts and strengthen their solidarity in the face of complex and constantly evolving regional challenges.

With the Mauritanian president, he addressed regional security and economic questions, with in-depth discussions on the situation in Palestine and the importance of strengthening bilateral cooperation.

These exchanges reflect President Guelleh's commitment to regional cooperation and stability, thus enriching the dialogues of the League of Arab States summit. The Djiboutian delegation, led by President Guelleh and composed of the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, and our ambassadors to Saudi Arabia and Egypt, respectively Dya Eddine Bamakhrama and Ahmed Ali Barreh, demonstrates the importance that the Republic of Djibouti attaches to these high-level discussions.

Indeed, the 33rd summit of the member countries of the Arab League came at a time when the Republic of Djibouti is in the running for the presidency of the African Union Commission.

Bahrain Declaration: Arab leaders reaffirm their commitment to peace and condemn Israeli aggression against the Gaza Strip

The leaders of the Arab States adopted a final declaration at the close of the 33rd Summit of the Council of Arab States in Bahrain, marking a renewed commitment to solidarity and prosperity in the region. Under the chairmanship of His Majesty the King of the Kingdom of Bahrain, the heads of state and government reaffirmed their bonds of fraternity and shared history, underlining the importance of collective action to preserve the security and stability of the Arab States.

The declaration highlights a common strategic vision to promote cooperation and integration in all fields, in the interest of the Arab peoples. The leaders also expressed their commitment to peace, tolerance and peaceful coexistence, while firmly condemning terrorism in all its forms.

A large part of the declaration is devoted to the Palestinian question, with an unequivocal condemnation of Israeli aggression against the Gaza Strip and an urgent call to put an end to this aggression, to lift the blockade and to allow the entry of humanitarian aid. The declaration also expressed solid support for countries such as Sudan, Syria, Yemen and Libya in their efforts to ensure stability, security and prosperity, while calling for political solutions in line with the aspirations of their peoples.

Finally, the Arab leaders committed to strengthening partnerships with international alliances and to cooperating with the United Nations to meet global challenges, including the achievement of the sustainable development goals by 2030.

The Bahrain Summit was hailed as an important step in promoting Arab solidarity and prosperity, illustrating the determination of Arab countries to overcome challenges and work together for a better future for the region. The final declaration reflects the deep commitment of the Arab States to strengthening their regional cooperation and meeting common challenges in a context of geopolitical upheaval and economic transformation.

a1076.t:
La chambre de commerce de Djibouti et une délégation d’hommes d’affaires indiens de la République de l’Inde ont signé mardi 21 janvier, un accord de partenariat commercial visant à faciliter la coopération et à renforcer les échanges commerciaux entre les deux pays.
La cérémonie de signature s’est déroulée en présence de M. Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, président de la chambre de commerce de Djibouti, M. Shiri Keivon, nouvel ambassadeur de la République de l’Inde, M. Isse Abdillahi Assoweh, ambassadeur de Djibouti en Inde, et M. Vishal P. Mehta, consul honoraire de la République de Djibouti à Bombay. La délégation comprenait également M. Nimish Ajmera, directeur des Groupements de Sociétés Indiens AJMERA, et M. Sanjay Ajmera, directeur de Ajmera Reality & Infra India Ltd. Cet accord marque une étape importante dans les échanges entre Djibouti et l’Inde, deux nations aux liens historiques et solides. L’objectif principal est de créer un environnement d’échanges commerciaux fluide et bénéfique pour les deux parties, tout en renforçant les relations économiques bilatérales et en attirant des investissements vers des projets à fort impact économique et social.
Dans un discours prononcé à cette occasion, M. Shiri Keivon, nouvel ambassadeur de l’Inde, s’est réjoui de participer à la signature de cet accord de partenariat, qui promet de renforcer les relations commerciales entre l’Inde et Djibouti. « C’est une grande réussite pour nos deux pays », a-t-il insisté.
De son côté, M. Isse Abdillahi Assoweh, ambassadeur de Djibouti en Inde, a exprimé sa gratitude envers le président de la chambre de commerce de Djibouti pour l’accueil chaleureux réservé à lui-même et à la délégation indienne d’hommes d’affaires. Il a souligné que le secteur public ne peut à lui seul soutenir la population et que la richesse vient du secteur privé. Prenant la parole à son tour, M. Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, président de la chambre de commerce de Djibouti, a souhaité la bienvenue à la délégation indienne à Djibouti. Il a exprimé sa joie de participer à cette cérémonie de signature d’accord entre la chambre de commerce de Djibouti et l’Inde. Il a rappelé ensuite les potentiels et les opportunités économiques de Djibouti ainsi que les échanges d’investissements, grâce à sa position géostratégique privilégiée par une plateforme logistique, portuaire, télécoms et d’infrastructures modernes au service de la région.
Le président de la chambre de commerce a également salué les efforts précieux des deux ambassades, l’Inde et Djibouti, pour leur travail acharné, qui a permis la concrétisation de cet accord de partenariat.
SOUBER
a1076.en:
The Djibouti chamber of commerce and a delegation of Indian businessmen from the Republic of India signed, on Tuesday 21 January, a commercial partnership agreement aimed at facilitating cooperation and strengthening trade between the two countries.

The signing ceremony took place in the presence of Mr Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, president of the Djibouti chamber of commerce, Mr Shiri Keivon, the new ambassador of the Republic of India, Mr Isse Abdillahi Assoweh, ambassador of Djibouti to India, and Mr Vishal P. Mehta, honorary consul of the Republic of Djibouti in Bombay. The delegation also included Mr Nimish Ajmera, director of the AJMERA Indian group of companies, and Mr Sanjay Ajmera, director of Ajmera Reality & Infra India Ltd. This agreement marks an important step in exchanges between Djibouti and India, two nations with historic and solid ties. The main objective is to create a smooth and mutually beneficial trading environment, while strengthening bilateral economic relations and attracting investment towards projects with a strong economic and social impact.

In a speech delivered on this occasion, Mr Shiri Keivon, the new ambassador of India, expressed his delight at taking part in the signing of this partnership agreement, which promises to strengthen commercial relations between India and Djibouti. "This is a great achievement for our two countries," he insisted.

For his part, Mr Isse Abdillahi Assoweh, ambassador of Djibouti to India, expressed his gratitude to the president of the Djibouti chamber of commerce for the warm welcome given to him and to the Indian delegation of businessmen. He stressed that the public sector cannot on its own support the population and that wealth comes from the private sector. Taking the floor in turn, Mr Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, president of the Djibouti chamber of commerce, welcomed the Indian delegation to Djibouti. He expressed his joy at taking part in this ceremony for the signing of an agreement between the Djibouti chamber of commerce and India. He then recalled Djibouti's economic potential and opportunities as well as investment exchanges, thanks to its privileged geostrategic position with a logistics, port, telecoms and modern infrastructure platform serving the region.

The president of the chamber of commerce also praised the valuable efforts of the two embassies, India and Djibouti, for their hard work, which made this partnership agreement possible.

SOUBER

Neue Produktionsstätte geplant
Deutsche Firma erstellt Studie für GH2 Projekte in Landesmitte
            
                        
                
            Swakopmund/Windhoek (bw) – In Zentralnamibia soll ein zweites großes „Tal“ für grünen Wasserstoff entstehen. Wie der Fonds für Umweltinvestition Namibias (EIF) diese Woche mitteilt, ist die deutsche Firma Fichtner GmbH & Co. aus Stuttgart damit beauftragt worden.
„Der EIF hat im Rahmen des Projekts „Green, Resilient Recovery Rapid Readiness Support in Namibia“ (NAM-RS-004) Fichtner beauftragt, die Machbarkeit der Produktion von grünem Wasserstoff und seiner Derivate in Namibia zu bewerten in dem (nach Lüderitz dem zweiten) geplanten ,,Wasserstoff-Tal“. Diese zentrale Region umfasst die drei Regionen Erongo, Khomas und Otjozondjupa,” teilte der EIF mit. Die Studie wird vom Grünen Klimafonds mit 300 000 US-Dollar finanziert.
Auch aus infrastruktureller Sicht sei die Landesmitte gut aufgestellt, da Straßen-, Bahn- und Hafenanlagen die drei (und weiter entfernte) Regionen miteinander verbinden. Ein weiterer Vorteil der Region seien die Solarressourcen.
„Es ist vorgesehen, dass diese Region zu einem „Drehkreuz“ für die Produktion von synthetischen Kraftstoffen und zugehörigen Produktionsanlagen für grüne Wasserstoffausrüstung wird”, so der EIF.
EIF-Vertreter und eine Mitarbeiterin von Fichtner statteten dem Erongo-Gouverneur Neville Andre kürzlich einen Höflichkeitsbesuch ab, um ihn über die Machbarkeitsstudie zu informieren.
Christina Mansfeld, eine Vertreterin von Fichtner, gab einen Überblick was die Studie alles beinhaltet, darunter Solar- und Wind-Potenzial sowie Produktionspotenzial für Wasserstoff und Wasserstoffderivate und die damit verbundenen geschätzten Produktionskosten.
„Die Studie zielt auch darauf ab, potenzielle Wegbereiter für eine wirtschaftliche und soziale Integration von grünem Wasserstoff und Derivaten für das zentrale Wasserstofftal zu bewerten”, hieß es.
„Es ist unbedingt erforderlich, die kumulativen negativen und positiven Umweltauswirkungen einzubeziehen, die sich aus zu vielen grünen Wasserstoffprojekten in einer Region ergeben,“ sagte Gouverneur Neville Andre. Namibias Regierung plant auch ein „Green Hydrogen Valley“ im Nordwesten der Kunene-Region.

„Es ist vorgesehen, dass diese Region zu einem „Drehkreuz“ für die Produktion von synthetischen Kraftstoffen und zugehörigen Produktionsanlagen für grüne Wasserstoffausrüstung wird”, so der EIF.

Christina Mansfeld, eine Vertreterin von Fichtner, gab einen Überblick was die Studie alles beinhaltet, darunter Solar- und Wind-Potenzial sowie Produktionspotenzial für Wasserstoff und Wasserstoffderivate und die damit verbundenen geschätzten Produktionskosten.
„Die Studie zielt auch darauf ab, potenzielle Wegbereiter für eine wirtschaftliche und soziale Integration von grünem Wasserstoff und Derivaten für das zentrale Wasserstofftal zu bewerten”, hieß es.
„Es ist unbedingt erforderlich, die kumulativen negativen und positiven Umweltauswirkungen einzubeziehen, die sich aus zu vielen grünen Wasserstoffprojekten in einer Region ergeben,“ sagte Gouverneur Neville Andre. Namibias Regierung plant auch ein „Green Hydrogen Valley“ im Nordwesten der Kunene-Region.
a1107.en:
New production facility planned
German firm draws up study for GH2 projects in the centre of the country

Swakopmund/Windhoek (bw) – A second large 'valley' for green hydrogen is to be created in central Namibia. As the Environmental Investment Fund of Namibia (EIF) announced this week, the German firm Fichtner GmbH & Co. of Stuttgart has been commissioned to do so.
"Under the project 'Green, Resilient Recovery Rapid Readiness Support in Namibia' (NAM-RS-004), the EIF has commissioned Fichtner to assess the feasibility of producing green hydrogen and its derivatives in Namibia in the planned 'hydrogen valley' (the second after Luederitz). This central region comprises the three regions of Erongo, Khomas and Otjozondjupa," the EIF said. The study is being financed by the Green Climate Fund with US$300,000.
From an infrastructure point of view too, the centre of the country is well positioned, since road, rail and port facilities connect the three (and more distant) regions with one another. Another advantage of the region is its solar resources.
"It is envisaged that this region will become a 'hub' for the production of synthetic fuels and associated production facilities for green hydrogen equipment," the EIF said.
EIF representatives and a member of staff from Fichtner recently paid a courtesy call on Erongo Governor Neville Andre to inform him about the feasibility study.
Christina Mansfeld, a representative of Fichtner, gave an overview of everything the study covers, including solar and wind potential as well as production potential for hydrogen and hydrogen derivatives and the associated estimated production costs.
"The study also aims to assess potential enablers for an economic and social integration of green hydrogen and derivatives for the central hydrogen valley," it was stated.
"It is absolutely essential to include the cumulative negative and positive environmental impacts that arise from too many green hydrogen projects in one region," said Governor Neville Andre. Namibia's government is also planning a 'Green Hydrogen Valley' in the north-west of the Kunene region.
