Occupied Jerusalem (INA) – The Palestine Monetary Authority released the results of its business cycle index for the current month of February, which showed the continued clear decline in the overall index during the month, against the backdrop of its contraction in both the West Bank and the Gaza Strip alike. As a result, the overall index fell to about -12.3 points compared with about -6.1 points in the previous month, and by about 1.0 point compared with February of last year. The Palestine Monetary Authority's business cycle index is a monthly index concerned with monitoring fluctuations in Palestinian economic activity by tracking the performance of industrial activity, and in particular fluctuations in levels of production and employment and their repercussions for the economy as a whole. The maximum value of the index is positive 100 points, while the minimum value is negative 100 points. A positive value indicates that economic conditions are good, whereas negative values indicate that economic conditions are bad.

The business cycle index in the West Bank settled in negative territory for the second consecutive quarter, recording about -5.1 points, compared with about -0.4 points in the previous month, as a result of the decline in the indices of some industrial activities, foremost among them the drop in the construction industries index, affected by the seasonal slowdown in construction activity, and the fall in the furniture industry index, alongside smaller declines in the leather industry and traditional industries indices. On the other side, the increases were limited: a rise in the food industry index, the plastics industry, and the engineering industries. It is worth noting that electricity prices rose at the beginning of the month by about 5% following an increase by the supplying Israeli company, something which appears to have left its mark on this month's indices. The results indicate that production and sales levels declined during the current month relative both to previous levels and to previously expected levels, according to what establishment owners reported. On the other hand, the level of optimism about the near future remains relatively high among establishment owners, who expressed greater confidence about the level of production and employment over the coming three months.

In the same vein, the deterioration in the Gaza Strip index continued, falling from -21.2 points to its lowest level since the Israeli war on the Gaza Strip in the summer of 2014, to about -35.1 points. The food industry index declined clearly, and the textile industry and construction industries indices fell. As is the case in the West Bank, the increases on the opposite side were limited: rises in the indices of the plastics industry, the chemical and pharmaceutical industries, and the furniture industry. On the other hand, establishment owners in Gaza pointed to a decline in the current volume of orders, which resulted in an accumulation of inventory, along with worsening pessimism about the near future, especially with regard to the level of employment. The Gaza Strip index is described as highly volatile, and in addition it has been treading water in negative territory, as has been the case for more than three years (with the exception of June 2015). The Strip faces a host of problems whose consequences weigh on the various economic sectors, and on the industrial sector in particular. These include the continuation of the economic blockade imposed by Israel, and the closure of the Rafah crossing except on rare occasions, along with the continued slowness of the Strip's reconstruction and the persistence of the electricity and fuel crisis without fundamental solutions. (End) Khaled Al-Khalidi / S J / H S

a6583.t:
L'USAID a financé le terrorisme en Afrique, déclare un membre du Congrès US
Boko Haram figure parmi les organisations terroristes subventionnées par l'Agence nationale de développement des États-Unis, a affirmé Scott Perry, représentant de la Pennsylvanie.
Ce mouvement est actif au Nigeria, au Cameroun, au Niger et au Tchad.
L'agence aurait dépensé 697 millions de dollars par an, sans compter les envois d'argent liquide, pour financer des organisations terroristes, dont Daech* et ISIS Khorasan, ainsi que leurs camps d'entraînement, a souligné l'élu républicain.
Il a fait cette déclaration au cours de l'audition inaugurale du DOGE (département de l'Efficacité gouvernementale) qui s'est tenue le 13 février.
L’USAID a été récemment fermée par l'administration Trump et fait l'objet d'un examen en raison d'allégations de mauvaise gestion et de gaspillage de l'argent des contribuables.
*Organisation terroriste interdite en Russie
a6583.en:
USAID funded terrorism in Africa, says a member of the US Congress

Boko Haram is among the terrorist organisations subsidised by the United States' national development agency, asserted Scott Perry, representative from Pennsylvania.

That movement is active in Nigeria, Cameroon, Niger and Chad.

The agency reportedly spent 697 million dollars a year, not counting shipments of cash, to finance terrorist organisations, including Daesh* and ISIS Khorasan, as well as their training camps, the Republican lawmaker stressed.

He made this statement during the inaugural hearing of DOGE (Department of Government Efficiency), held on 13 February.

USAID was recently shut down by the Trump administration and is under review over allegations of mismanagement and waste of taxpayers' money.

*Terrorist organisation banned in Russia

a6689.t:
President Nangolo Mbumba has appealed to the United Nations General Assembly to support the modalities to actualize the advisory opinion rendered by the International Court of Justice regarding the ongoing conflict in Gaza.
The International Court of Justice, in its advisory opinion, stated that Israel's continued occupation of the Gaza Strip and West Bank is a violation of international law.
The advisory opinion further outlined that Israel end the war, but in spite of this, attacks continue, leaving thousands destitute.
"Prolonged occupation does not justify or make acceptable the hardships and injustices endured. This is particularly true for the people of Gaza, who continue to be brutally massacred. As a country that has endured genocide, Namibia believes that Israel, by intent and by action, is committing genocide. Namibia continues to call for a ceasefire and for humanitarian assistance to flow unhindered into Gaza."
President Mbumba additionally repeated Namibia's call for the lifting of decades' old US blockades against Cuba and Zimbabwe.
"Economic hardships continue to affect the sister Republic of Cuba, in stark contrast to the ideals of inclusivity and the goal of leaving no one behind. Namibia calls for the end of the economic, financial, and commercial blockade against Cuba. Namibia also reiterates its call for the immediate and unconditional lifting of illegal sanctions against Zimbabwe, which hinders the country's capacity to achieve Sustainable Development Goals."
The quest for self-determination for the Sahrawi people remains a matter that the Namibian leader says the world body should help intensify.
Dr. Mbumba reminded the Assembly that continued disenfranchisement of the people of Western Sahara is an affront to the UN Charter, its purposes and principles, and that this year's session must change this.

a6744.t:
Dès sa prise de fonction, le Président Obama s'est engagé à soutenir des gouvernements stables, ouverts et responsables, ainsi que le développement durable en Afrique.
Dans son discours prononcé devant le Parlement ghanéen en juillet 2009, le Président a affirmé que l'Afrique est une partie fondamentale de notre monde interconnecté, et a souhaité un partenariat avec l'Afrique qui soit "fondé sur la responsabilité mutuelle et le respect mutuel". La Stratégie de sécurité nationale, publiée en mai 2010, renforce cette vision et milite en faveur d'un partenariat avec les nations africaines au moment où elles développent leurs économies et renforcent leurs institutions démocratiques et leur gouvernance. En juin 2012, le Président a approuvé une Directive de politique présidentielle qui définit sa vision sur la politique américaine à l'égard de l'Afrique subsaharienne. Le présent document s'inspire de cette directive et la reflète.
Les économies de l'Afrique subsaharienne sont celles qui ont le plus fort taux de croissance dans le monde. Un nombre croissant de gouvernements africains et d'organisations régionales jouent un rôle prépondérant dans la gestion des défis sécuritaires et politiques à l'intérieur de leurs frontières et à l'extérieur et ils sont de plus en plus des acteurs influents de la scène internationale. L'Union africaine joue un rôle principal dans les questions politiques, diplomatiques et de maintien de la paix sur le continent. Parallèlement, l'urbanisation et une population jeune bourgeonnante transforment la société de manière profonde et les jeunes gens font de plus en plus entendre leurs voix.
Bien que le continent ait réalisé des succès en démocratie et dans la mise en place des institutions, ces gains demeurent fragiles. Il reste encore cependant de nombreux pays où la transition vers la démocratie est difficile et lente et il y a des leaders qui refusent de renoncer au pouvoir. Dans de nombreux pays, la corruption est endémique et les institutions étatiques sont faibles. En plus de l'érosion de la légitimité des gouvernements, ces facteurs nuisent à l'entrepreneuriat local et aux investissements étrangers. Malgré qu'ils disposent d'une grande partie des terres arables du monde et des ressources halieutiques abondantes, de nombreux États de l'Afrique subsaharienne se caractérisent par un secteur agricole peu performant et une pauvreté qui menace toujours inutilement la vie des populations. Les défis sécuritaires transnationaux constituent des menaces pour la stabilité de la région, la croissance économique et les intérêts américains.
Étant donné l'importance stratégique grandissante de l'Afrique subsaharienne pour les États-Unis, au cours des cinq prochaines années, nous redirigerons nos efforts et les multiplieront en vue de renforcer les institutions démocratiques et booster la croissance économique, le commerce et les investissements, tout en continuant à poursuivre d'autres objectifs sur le continent. Des institutions démocratiques plus fortes permettent aux États de réaliser une plus grande stabilité et prospérité durable; réussissent mieux dans la réduction des conflits et des menaces transfrontalières; et constituent des partenaires forts pour les États-Unis. En outre, promouvoir une croissance économique durable et inclusive est un élément clé de la sécurité, de la stabilité politique et du développement, et constitue par conséquent le ferment des efforts visant la réduction de la pauvreté par le biais de la création de ressources qui soutiennent les soins de santé, l'éducation et les biens publics.
Compte tenu de ce qui précède, les Etats-Unis ont mis au point une stratégie à quatre piliers au titre de sa politique à l’égard de l’Afrique sub-saharienne. Il s’agi d’une stratégie novatrice qui consiste à collaborer avec les pays de l'Afrique subsaharienne pour renforcer les institutions démocratiques; stimuler la croissance économique, le commerce et les investissements; promouvoir la paix et la sécurité ; promouvoir les opportunités et le développement. Pour l’atteinte de ces objectifs, une place de choix sera accordée à la jeunesse en approfondissant la collaboration avec les jeunes leaders africains.
Renforcer les institutions démocratiques
Comme le Président Obama l'avait déclaré au Ghana, "l'Afrique n'a pas besoin d’hommes forts, mais d'institutions fortes". Comme il a été mentionné dans la Stratégie de sécurité nationale, le soutien à la démocratie est d'une importance capitale pour les intérêts des États-Unis et constitue un élément fondamental de l'intervention américaine à l'étranger. Par conséquent, la mise en œuvre d’ une série d’actions s’avère indispensable, à savoir : la Promotion d’une gouvernance responsable, transparente et sensible dans le sens d’un soutien accru aux capacités des principaux réformateurs et institutions gouvernementales à tous les niveaux ; la Valorisation des modèles positifs, c’est à dire les leaders et les acteurs qui créent des modèles démocratiques viables, y compris les dirigeants élus, ainsi que les jeunes Africains qui sont des leaders de la société civile et dans l'entrepreneuriat ; la promotion et la protection des droits de l'homme, de la société civile et d’une presse indépendante ; le maintien d’une convergence soutenue sur la crédibilité des processus démocratiques et la Promotion des normes démocratiques fortes.
Stimuler la croissance économique, le commerce et les investissements
Les États-Unis ont intérêt à améliorer la compétitivité commerciale de la région, à encourager la diversification des exportations au-delà des ressources naturelles et à s'assurer que les retombées de la croissance sont accessibles aux populations. Les actions ci-après seront menées, par le biais du commerce et les investissements : la Promotion d’un environnement favorable au commerce et aux investissements ; l’amélioration de la gouvernance économique ; la promotion de l'intégration régionale ; l’augmentation de la capacité de l'Afrique à accéder effectivement aux marchés internationaux et d’en tirer profit et l’encouragement des entreprises américaines à investir en Afrique et à y faire du commerce.
Promouvoir la paix et la sécurité
Les pays africains font preuve de capacités croissantes pour impulser la gestion des questions de sécurité sur le continent. Cependant, les conflits au niveau interne et international, ainsi que l'incapacité de certains gouvernements à satisfaire les besoins de sécurité de base de leurs populations continuent à constituer des obstacles clés à l'effectivité de la gouvernance démocratique, de la croissance économique, du commerce et des investissements, ainsi que du développement humain. Seuls les gouvernements africains et leurs populations peuvent résoudre de manière durable les défis sécuritaires et les divisions internes qui minent le continent, bien que les États-Unis peuvent influencer positivement. Conscient de ce fait, les actions suivantes seront menées : la Lutte contre Al-qaeda et d'autres groupes terroristes pour qu’en conformité avec la Stratégie de sécurité nationale pour la lutte contre le terrorisme, les Etats-Unis puissent concentrer leurs efforts sur la rupture, le démantèlement et éventuellement la défaite d'Al-qaeda, de ses affiliés et adhérents en Afrique en vue d'assurer la sécurité des citoyens Américains et de leurs partenaires africains; la Promotion de la coopération en matière de sécurité régionale et la réforme du secteur sécuritaire ; la Prévention des menaces criminelles transfrontalières ; la Prévention des conflits et, si nécessaire, l’atténuation des atrocités de masse et la traduction des auteurs devant les tribunaux pour répondre de leurs actes ; un soutien accru aux initiatives de promotion de la paix et de la sécurité.
Promouvoir les opportunités et le développement
Le présent gouvernement, par l’entremise de la Directive présidentielle sur le développement global, a développé une nouvelle approche qui met l'accent sur le développement durable, ainsi qu'un nouveau modèle opérationnel pour l'aide américaine au développement qui se fonde sur les réalisations actuelles. L'Afrique est au centre de trois principales initiatives de développement du Président Obama, à savoir: l'Initiative mondiale en matière de santé, Nourrir l'avenir, et l'Initiative mondiale pour la lutte contre le changement climatique. En outre, deux des quatre pays du Partenariat pour la croissance (le Ghana et la Tanzanie) se trouvent en Afrique. Dans le cadre de chacun de ces efforts, les Etats-Unis ont souligné l'importance de la réforme et de la transparence pour le développement et un accent a été mis sur la bonne gestion de l'économie et des projets en vue de promouvoir la durabilité. Les Etats-Unis investissent dans un nombre croissant de pays de grande performance et les résultats sont visibles au travers d'une plus grande capacité et d'un engagement plus accru des partenaires. Les actions ci-après seront menées pour atteindre cet objectif :
La suppression des contraintes à la croissance et la promotion de la réduction de la pauvreté ; la promotion de la sécurité alimentaire ; la transformation de la santé publique en Afrique ; l’accroissement des opportunités en faveur des femmes et de la jeunesse ; la réaction aux crises humanitaires tout en promouvant la résilience ; la promotion d’une croissance à faible émission de gaz et le développement durable et la résilience aux changements climatiques.
a6744.en:
Strategy of the United States of America towards sub-Saharan Africa

From the moment he took office, President Obama committed himself to supporting stable, open and accountable governments, as well as sustainable development in Africa.

In his speech delivered before the Ghanaian Parliament in July 2009, the President affirmed that Africa is a fundamental part of our interconnected world, and called for a partnership with Africa "founded on mutual responsibility and mutual respect". The National Security Strategy, published in May 2010, reinforces this vision and argues in favour of a partnership with African nations as they develop their economies and strengthen their democratic institutions and their governance. In June 2012, the President approved a Presidential Policy Directive which sets out his vision for American policy towards sub-Saharan Africa. The present document draws on that directive and reflects it.

The economies of sub-Saharan Africa are those with the highest growth rates in the world. A growing number of African governments and regional organisations are playing a leading role in managing security and political challenges within and beyond their borders, and they are increasingly influential actors on the international stage. The African Union plays a leading role in political, diplomatic and peacekeeping matters on the continent. At the same time, urbanisation and a burgeoning young population are transforming society in profound ways, and young people are increasingly making their voices heard.

Although the continent has achieved successes in democracy and in the establishment of institutions, these gains remain fragile. There nevertheless remain many countries where the transition to democracy is difficult and slow, and there are leaders who refuse to relinquish power. In many countries corruption is endemic and state institutions are weak. In addition to eroding the legitimacy of governments, these factors harm local entrepreneurship and foreign investment. Despite possessing a large share of the world's arable land and abundant fisheries resources, many states of sub-Saharan Africa are characterised by a poorly performing agricultural sector and by poverty that still needlessly threatens the lives of the population. Transnational security challenges constitute threats to the region's stability, to economic growth and to American interests.

Given the growing strategic importance of sub-Saharan Africa for the United States, over the next five years we will redirect our efforts and multiply them with a view to strengthening democratic institutions and boosting economic growth, trade and investment, while continuing to pursue other objectives on the continent. Stronger democratic institutions enable states to achieve greater stability and lasting prosperity; they are more successful in reducing conflicts and cross-border threats; and they constitute strong partners for the United States. Furthermore, promoting sustainable and inclusive economic growth is a key element of security, political stability and development, and therefore constitutes the seedbed of efforts aimed at reducing poverty through the creation of resources that support health care, education and public goods.

In light of the foregoing, the United States has devised a four-pillar strategy as part of its policy towards sub-Saharan Africa. It is an innovative strategy which consists of collaborating with the countries of sub-Saharan Africa to strengthen democratic institutions; to stimulate economic growth, trade and investment; to promote peace and security; and to promote opportunity and development. In order to achieve these objectives, pride of place will be given to youth by deepening collaboration with young African leaders.

Strengthening democratic institutions

As President Obama had declared in Ghana, "Africa does not need strongmen, it needs strong institutions". As was mentioned in the National Security Strategy, support for democracy is of capital importance for the interests of the United States and constitutes a fundamental element of American engagement abroad. Consequently, the implementation of a series of actions proves indispensable, namely: the promotion of accountable, transparent and responsive governance in the sense of increased support for the capacities of key reformers and governmental institutions at all levels; the highlighting of positive models, that is to say the leaders and actors who create viable democratic models, including elected leaders as well as young Africans who are leaders in civil society and in entrepreneurship; the promotion and protection of human rights, of civil society and of an independent press; the maintenance of a sustained convergence on the credibility of democratic processes; and the promotion of strong democratic norms.

Stimulating economic growth, trade and investment

The United States has an interest in improving the region's commercial competitiveness, in encouraging the diversification of exports beyond natural resources, and in ensuring that the benefits of growth are accessible to the population. The following actions will be carried out, by means of trade and investment: the promotion of an environment favourable to trade and investment; the improvement of economic governance; the promotion of regional integration; the increase of Africa's capacity to access international markets effectively and to profit from them; and the encouragement of American businesses to invest in Africa and to trade there.

Promoting peace and security

African countries are demonstrating growing capacities to drive the management of security matters on the continent. However, internal and international conflicts, as well as the inability of some governments to satisfy the basic security needs of their populations, continue to constitute key obstacles to the effectiveness of democratic governance, of economic growth, trade and investment, and of human development. Only African governments and their populations can sustainably resolve the security challenges and internal divisions that undermine the continent, although the United States can exert a positive influence. Conscious of this fact, the following actions will be carried out: the fight against Al-Qaeda and other terrorist groups so that, in conformity with the National Security Strategy for counterterrorism, the United States can concentrate its efforts on the disruption, dismantling and eventual defeat of Al-Qaeda, its affiliates and adherents in Africa, with a view to ensuring the security of American citizens and of their African partners; the promotion of regional security cooperation and of security sector reform; the prevention of cross-border criminal threats; the prevention of conflicts and, where necessary, the mitigation of mass atrocities and the bringing of perpetrators before the courts to answer for their acts; and increased support for initiatives promoting peace and security.

Promoting opportunity and development

The present administration, by means of the Presidential Directive on Global Development, has developed a new approach which emphasises sustainable development, as well as a new operating model for American development assistance which builds on current achievements. Africa is at the centre of three of President Obama's main development initiatives, namely: the Global Health Initiative, Feed the Future, and the Global Climate Change Initiative. In addition, two of the four Partnership for Growth countries (Ghana and Tanzania) are in Africa. Within each of these efforts, the United States has emphasised the importance of reform and transparency for development, and an emphasis has been placed on sound management of the economy and of projects with a view to promoting sustainability. The United States is investing in a growing number of high-performing countries and the results are visible through greater capacity and a stronger commitment on the part of partners. The following actions will be carried out to achieve this objective:

The removal of constraints to growth and the promotion of poverty reduction; the promotion of food security; the transformation of public health in Africa; the increase of opportunities for women and youth; the response to humanitarian crises while promoting resilience; and the promotion of low-emissions growth and of sustainable development and resilience to climate change.

a6819.t:
Men of various ages marched through Rundu as part of the 16 Days of Activism, which aims to create awareness of gender-based violence.
The "Commitment Walk" aims to encourage men to adopt respectful, non-violent, and reasonable behaviour in relationships.
Led by the Kavango East Governor, Bonifatius Wakudumo, the men walked from the Rundu Sports Stadium, through the CBD, and ended up at the Governor's office for a programme filled with advice on how to become better men in society.
Johannes Mururani told the group he was a violent man until he attended a male engagement programme on gender norms under the USAID Reach Namibia Project. He is now adamant about creating a safe environment.
"Imagine a world where boys and girls can walk safely to school without fear of violence. A world where women can make decisions about their health and bodies without coercion. A world where men and women stand together as equals, united in the fight against gender-based violence and HIV."
According to Katamba Nanyemba, the project coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project, there is ample evidence linking gender-based violence and HIV.
"It shows us that survivors of violence have often limited control over their sexual health, face power imbalances that prevent them from negotiating safer sex, and fear stigma that deters them from accessing critical services."
The Kavango East Governor told the group that it is their duty as men to educate themselves and others about GBV, its root causes, and its impact on individuals.
"It is believed that five in six men are not abusers. But where are they? Can they stand up and be counted? Can the one in six who are abusers change their ways? Can we raise a new generation based on equality? Change is not easy, and it does not happen overnight. But every step we take today is a step toward building a safer and more equitable future. Let us be unwavering in our commitment and courageous in our actions."
Men also had the opportunity to access sexual reproductive health services and sign pledges for the fight against GBV.
The event was organised by IntraHealth Namibia through the USAID-funded Reach Namibia Project.

a6860.t:
A recent report by SwissAid has alleged that some gold from South Sudan, Ethiopia, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and possibly Sudan passes through Kenya before being re-exported to Dubai, where it is finally declared for import.
Released late last month, the report reveals that over the past decade, Kenya has grown into a popular smuggling hub for gold, primarily destined for the United Arab Emirates (UAE), particularly Dubai.
According to SwissAid, illicit gold outflows from Kenya likely exceed two tons per year, while declared gold exports were only 672 kilograms in 2023. The report notes that the vast majority of gold entering the country leaves without being officially declared for export.
The report partly stated: “Part of the gold that is smuggled out of South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and, to a lesser extent, Ethiopia, and possibly Sudan, passes through Kenya before being re-exported. Most of the gold smuggled out of Kenya is shipped to Dubai and declared for import there.”
SwissAid further stated that, based on interviews with industry experts and government records, declared gold exports from Kenya often exceed the country’s known gold production and declared imports. This discrepancy leads the NGO to conclude that inbound illicit gold flows are occurring.
The report also highlights that the two licensed medium-scale mines responsible for Kenya’s declared gold production export their material to refiners located in South Africa and Switzerland.
Additionally, reports have surfaced alleging secret gold transactions involving Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces (RSF), suggesting that Sudanese gold is transported through Jomo Kenyatta International Airport en route to Dubai.
In response to growing gold smuggling concerns, Kenya is planning to establish a Mining Police Unit and is advocating for regional certification of gems.
On Monday, June 9, 2025, South Sudan’s Ministry of Mining called for an urgent crackdown on rampant gold smuggling at Juba International Airport, describing the illicit trade as a “major challenge” to the nation.
Matiok Santino Akuei, Undersecretary in the Ministry of Mining, emphasized the negative impact of the illicit mineral trade on the ministry’s operations. He stated,
“The smuggling of gold and precious minerals has become a great challenge for the Republic of South Sudan, undermining our performance.”
Akuei urged law enforcement agencies and relevant stakeholders to immediately report any suspicious activities related to mineral smuggling. He stressed that the Ministry of Mining holds the sole mandate to license all gold and mineral exports.
He warned that any mineral export without proper authorization is illegal and could lead to arrest and prosecution.
To tackle the issue, the ministry recently held a crucial meeting with national and international partners.
Although not fully controlled by the government, the gold mining industry employs tens of thousands of artisanal miners. The majority of these miners are unregistered and operate illegally, despite laws requiring registration with the Ministry of Mining to assign specific mining areas.
This lack of registration complicates monitoring and enforcement of mining regulations.
Locals often use crude traditional methods and equipment to extract gravel and soil, then pan for small gold particles using water. However, the law clearly states that all unlicensed mining activities, including artisanal mining, are illegal.
Many local miners, who have been mining for generations, are unaware of the government’s mandate to regulate the sector.
Across mining sites in South Sudan, government institutions are largely absent, resulting in a lack of monitoring, sensitization, consultation, conflict prevention, and support.
Mining communities feel neglected and believe the government prioritizes company operations over artisanal miners’ welfare.
In 2020, the Bank of South Sudan announced plans to purchase crude gold locally to boost the economy, focusing on Kapoeta, where thousands of artisanal miners operate. However, the plan failed as local miners preferred selling their gold to Somali nationals, who offered prices above the government’s fixed rates.
In South Sudan, local buyers purchase gold from miners and sell it to larger dealers in regional towns such as Kapoeta. From there, dealers transport the gold to Juba by air or road, or across borders to Uganda or Kenya.
Most gold produced in South Sudan is smuggled out of the country. The main supply routes run through Uganda and Kenya and also reach the DRC and Sudan. Many consignments are flown out of Juba.
The gold’s direction largely depends on the nearest border crossings, with Nimule-Elegu and Kaya (towards Uganda) and Nakodok (towards Kenya) being key border posts. Air shipments from Juba primarily head to Kampala, Dubai, and China.

a6878.t:
Le projet d’employabilité de la main d’œuvre Djiboutienne (PED), financé par le gouvernement des Etats Unis à travers l’USAID, a organisé une formation des formateurs/trices du 18 au 21 novembre 2019 au CRIPEN. La session de formation a été clôturée, jeudi dernier,en présence des hauts cadres du MENFOP et des responsables du PED.
La formation avait pour objectif d’introduire les programmes du PED sur les « Compétences de base en Employabilité et en Entrepreneuriat (CBEE) » et « Apprentissage en milieu professionnel » aux concepteurs du programme « Découverte des métiers » du MENFOP qui sera enseigné durant les quatre années du collège à partir de l’année scolaire 2020/21. La conception de ce nouveau programme figure dans la réforme de l’enseignement de base et moyen qui est en cours.
Cette formation de cinq jours a vu la participation des concepteurs de programmes d’enseignement du CRIPEN. Dans le cadre de cette formation, les participant(e)s ont pris part à différentes activités pratiques issues des programmes sur les CBEE et « Apprentissage en milieu professionnels » pour une éventuelle intégration de certaines activités dans les matériels pédagogiques de l’enseignement général.
Les sujets traités par ces programmes comprennent : fixer et atteindre des objectifs, l’auto-analyse des lacunes en compétences et les styles d’apprentissage, la communication interpersonnelle, la proactivité, la collaboration en équipe, comprendre ce que c’est que le « travail » et la découverte des métiers et lieux de travail dans votre communauté. D’autre part, plusieurs discussions accentuées sur l’approche participative que devra avoir le programme « Découverte des métiers » ont été menées.
Le directeur général du CRIPEN, Saïd Nour Hassan, la secrétaire exécutive de l’éducation, Ayan Osman, l’inspectrice générale de l’enseignement général, Mouna Ismaïl la cheffe de projet du PED, Laura Dillon- Binkley, et les responsables du PED ont tous pris part à la cérémonie de clôture de cette formation et ont respectivement évoqué leur enthousiasme par rapport à la création d’un tel programme qui pourra faciliter aux jeunes leur choix de filière et qui déterminera par conséquent leur choix de carrière.
Plus généralement, les concepteurs de programme du CRIPEN, les conseillers pédagogiques et les inspecteurs du MENFOP, qui ont suivi cette formation, ont vu leurs compétences nettement renforcées sur notamment les approches participatives, mais aussi la meilleure manière de découvrir les métiers ou le travail à travers les modules de l’organisation Education Developement Center (EDC). Le soutien du gouvernement américain à travers le projet d’employabilité de la main d’œuvre djiboutienne est destiné à soutenir le MENFOP vers une amélioration de la qualité des programmes pour avoir des jeunes qui maîtrisent les compétences douces et techniques et sont capables de répondre à tous les défis du marché du travail.
Aussi, la commission de rédaction des curricula bénéficiera d’un soutien pour l’élaboration du module de découverte des métiers pour qu’ils puissent être outillés à travers l’intégration de quelques activités de nos modules à ce programme. L’apport est inestimable car nos modules sont axés sur le développement et la communication interpersonnelle, le leadership et l’introduction au monde du travail, etc. Tout cela va guider les jeunes à avoir une meilleure connaissance d’eux-mêmes et de leurs compétences à partir de la classe de 6ème année, ainsi ils seront prêts à affronter le monde et mieux appréhender leurs métiers de demain.
Ce projet est un autre exemple du partenariat fort entre les gouvernements des Etats-Unis et de Djibouti pour améliorer l’emploi des Djiboutiens et en particulier les jeunes.
Le point avec…Ahmed Moussa Ahmed
Spécialiste en éducation formelle au PED
L’objectif de cette formation des formateur-trices était d’introduire le programme des compétences de base en employabilité et en entreprenariat et du programme d’apprentissage en milieu professionnel aux concepteurs de curricula et des conseillers pédagogiques pour le nouveau programme sur la découverte de métier destinés aux élèves de l’enseignement moyen de l’enseignement général. Parmi les bénéficiaires, un comité de rédaction va siéger pour réfléchir sur les modules, les activités qui font être utilisées afin de produire un programme sur la découverte des métiers, un nouveau programme que le MENFOP souhaite mettre en place dès la classe de sixième au collège. Durant cette formation des formateur-trices, les bénéficiaires ont acquis les approches participatives de la formation. Ils ont été amenés à faire des cas pratiques d’entretien informatifs avec les entreprises proches du CRIPEN et ont pu exercer des activités comportementales.
MAS
a6878.en:
USAID's DJIBOUTIAN WORKFORCE EMPLOYABILITY PROJECT (PED): Training of trainers for curriculum writers

The Djiboutian Workforce Employability Project (PED), funded by the United States government through USAID, organised a training of trainers from 18 to 21 November 2019 at CRIPEN. The training session was closed last Thursday in the presence of senior officials of MENFOP and PED managers.

The aim of the training was to introduce the PED programmes on "Core Employability and Entrepreneurship Skills (CBEE)" and "Work-based Learning" to the designers of MENFOP's "Discovery of Occupations" programme, which will be taught throughout the four years of middle school starting from the 2020/21 school year. The design of this new programme is part of the ongoing reform of basic and middle education.

This five-day training saw the participation of CRIPEN's curriculum designers. Within the framework of this training, the participants took part in various practical activities drawn from the CBEE and "Work-based Learning" programmes, with a view to the possible integration of some activities into the teaching materials of general education.

The subjects covered by these programmes include: setting and achieving goals, self-analysis of skills gaps and learning styles, interpersonal communication, proactivity, team collaboration, understanding what "work" is, and discovering occupations and workplaces in your community. In addition, several discussions were held with emphasis on the participatory approach that the "Discovery of Occupations" programme should have.

The director general of CRIPEN, Said Nour Hassan, the executive secretary for education, Ayan Osman, the inspector general of general education, Mouna Ismail, the head of the PED project, Laura Dillon-Binkley, and PED officials all took part in the closing ceremony of this training and each expressed their enthusiasm about the creation of such a programme, which will be able to make it easier for young people to choose their stream and which will consequently determine their career choice.

More generally, the CRIPEN curriculum designers, the pedagogical advisers and the MENFOP inspectors who took this training saw their skills clearly strengthened, particularly on participatory approaches, but also on the best way to discover occupations or work through the modules of the Education Development Center (EDC) organisation. The American government's support through the Djiboutian workforce employability project is intended to support MENFOP towards an improvement in the quality of programmes, so as to have young people who master soft and technical skills and are able to meet all the challenges of the labour market.

Also, the curriculum drafting commission will receive support for the development of the occupation-discovery module so that they can be equipped through the integration of some activities of our modules into this programme. The contribution is invaluable because our modules focus on development and interpersonal communication, leadership and introduction to the world of work, etc. All this will guide young people towards a better knowledge of themselves and of their skills from the 6th grade onwards, so that they will be ready to face the world and to better understand their occupations of tomorrow.

This project is another example of the strong partnership between the governments of the United States and Djibouti to improve the employment of Djiboutians, and in particular of young people.

A word with... Ahmed Moussa Ahmed
Specialist in formal education at PED

The objective of this training of trainers was to introduce the core employability and entrepreneurship skills programme and the work-based learning programme to curriculum designers and pedagogical advisers for the new programme on the discovery of occupations intended for pupils of middle school in general education. Among the beneficiaries, a drafting committee will sit to reflect on the modules and the activities to be used in order to produce a programme on the discovery of occupations, a new programme that MENFOP wishes to put in place from the sixth grade in middle school. During this training of trainers, the beneficiaries acquired the participatory approaches of training. They were led to carry out practical cases of informational interviews with companies near CRIPEN and were able to practise behavioural activities.

MAS

a7255.t:
Muktasari:
- Wadau hao wakiwemo kutoka serikalini, sekta binafsi na wadau wa maendeleo, watajadiliana namna ya kuboresha mifumo endelevu ya chakula ikiwemo ushirikishwaji wa jamii na namna ya kukabiliana na mabadiliko ya tabia nchi.
Arusha. Wadau kutoka taasisi za Serikali, mashirika ya umoja wa mataifa, sekta binafsi wamekutana kwa siku mbili jijini Arsuaha katika warsha ya kujadili namna ya kuboresha mifumo ya chakula nchini.
Wadau hao wamekutana kuanzia leo Alhamisi Mei 29, 2025 ambapo pamoja na masuala mengine watajadili namna ya kuongeza uelewa wa kina wa mifumo ya chakula na kuendeleza mifumo hiyo ikiwemo ushirikishwaji wa jamii na namna ya kukabiliana na mabadiliko ya tabia nchi.
Akizungumza katika warsha hiyo, Mwakilishi na Mkurugenzi Mkazi wa Mfuko wa Kimataifa wa Maendeleo ya Kilimo (IFAD), Sakphouseth Meng amesema kilimo ni sekta muhimu kwa uchumi wa Tanzania ikichangia asilimia 29.1 ya pato la Taifa huku ikiaajiri zaidi ya asilimia 65 ya watu wote.
Amesema wanakutana hapo kwa lengo la kuleta mabadiliko ya mifumo ya chakula nchini kuanzia uzalishaji na usambazaji wa chakula, kulinda mazingira na kushughulikia changamoto kama vile utapiamlo na mabadiliko ya tabia nchi.
"Kilimo bado ni sekta muhimu kwa uchumi wa Tanzania, kwa hiyo mabadiliko yake ni muhimu kwa ukuaji wa kilimo na kwa ustawi na ustawi wa Watanzania wote. Na tangu mwaka 2021 Tanzania imekuwa ikitumia jitihada mbalimbali za Kimataifa kurekebisha mifumo yake ya chakula,”
"Mabadiliko haya yanahitaji uwekezaji katika kilimo kinachozingatia mabadiliko ya tabia nchi. Mabadiliko ya mifumo ya chakula inahitaji ushirikiano, uwekezaji wa kimkakati kutoka kwa wadau wote," amesema.
Mwakilishi huyo amesema mpango wa kuendeleza mifumo endelevu ya chakula unaotekelezwa na Shirika la Chakula Duniani (Fao), Shirika la Umoja wa Mataifa la Mpango wa Chakula Duniani (WFP) na Ifad umelenga kusaidia kuimarisha mifumo ya chakula Tanzania na kuvutia uwekezaji.
Awali Naibu Katibu Mkuu kutoka Wizara ya Uvuvi na Mifugo, Abdul Mhinte, amesema kuna miradi miwili inafadhiliwa na wadau mbalimbali wakiwemo Ifad inayogharimu zaidi ya Dola za Marekani milioni 200.
Amesema miradi hiyo miwili ya miaka mitano inatekelezwa hapa nchini kuanzia mwaka huu 2025 ni miradi inayoshughulika na masuala ya maziwa na uvuvi.
"Lengo la miradi hii miwili ni kukuza uzalishaji na kuangalia mifumo mizima ya uzalishaji wa vyakula katika maeneo hayo, kuanzia inavyozalishwa hadi inapomfikia mlaji hasa kwa kuzingatia mabadiliko ya tabia nchi," amesema.
Naibu huyo amesema Tanzania inajitosheleza kwa chakula licha ya baadhi ya kaya hasa za vijijini kutokana na sababu mbalimbali na kuwa miradi kama hiyo inasaidia kuboresha mifumo ya chakula ili kuona kinawafikia walaji vikiwa na ubora unaostahili, vitoe lishe inayokusudiwa kwenye afya ya binadamu.
Ofisa Kilimo Mkuu kutoka Wizara ya Kilimo, Margaret Natai aliyemwakilisha Mratibu wa mifumo ya chakula nchini, amesema wao kama wizara wanashirikiana na wadau wengine ili kutekeleza mikakati ya kuhakikisha mifumo endelevu ya chakula nchini inatekelezeka.
Amesema mwaka 2021 waliandaa malengo katika sekta mbalimbali na wanayo miongozo inayowaongoza ikiwemo kuangalia usalama wa chakula, ulishaji wa watoto shuleni, upotevu wa chakula na usindikaji.
"Kutokana na hayo kila mdau hapa ana nafasi ya kushiriki na kikao cha leo tunaelimisha wadau waelewe namna ya kujipanga kufikia malengo ikiwemo namna ya kutumia teknolojia bunifu katika uzalishaji," amesema Ofisa huyo.
Mkurugenzi wa Idara ya Maendeleo ya Mifugo kutoka Wizara ya Kilimo, Umwagiliaji Maliasili na Mifugo Zanzibar, Asha Zahran Mohamed amesema warsha hiyo itawasaidia kutoa elimu kwa wananchi katika kuboresha mifumo ya chakula, uzalishaji wa nyama na maziwa.
a7255.en:
Summary:
- These stakeholders, including those from government, the private sector and development partners, will discuss how to improve sustainable food systems, including community involvement and how to cope with climate change.

Arusha. Stakeholders from government institutions, United Nations agencies and the private sector have met for two days in the city of Arusha in a workshop to discuss how to improve the country's food systems.

These stakeholders have been meeting since today, Thursday May 29, 2025, where, among other matters, they will discuss how to increase a deep understanding of food systems and to develop those systems, including community involvement and how to cope with climate change.

Speaking at the workshop, the Representative and Country Director of the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), Sakphouseth Meng, said agriculture is an important sector for Tanzania's economy, contributing 29.1 percent of the national GDP while employing more than 65 percent of all people.

He said they are meeting there with the aim of bringing about a transformation of the country's food systems, from the production and distribution of food, to protecting the environment and tackling challenges such as malnutrition and climate change.

"Agriculture is still an important sector for Tanzania's economy, so its transformation is important for the growth of agriculture and for the welfare and prosperity of all Tanzanians. And since 2021 Tanzania has been drawing on various international efforts to reform its food systems,"

"This transformation requires investment in climate-smart agriculture. The transformation of food systems requires cooperation and strategic investment from all stakeholders," he said.

That Representative said the programme for developing sustainable food systems, which is implemented by the Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) and IFAD, is aimed at helping to strengthen Tanzania's food systems and to attract investment.

Earlier, the Deputy Permanent Secretary from the Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries, Abdul Mhinte, said there are two projects funded by various stakeholders, including IFAD, costing more than 200 million US dollars.

He said those two five-year projects, being implemented here in the country starting this year, 2025, are projects dealing with dairy and fisheries matters.

"The goal of these two projects is to boost production and to look at the entire systems of food production in those areas, from how it is produced until it reaches the consumer, especially taking into account climate change," he said.

The Deputy Permanent Secretary said Tanzania is self-sufficient in food, despite some households, especially rural ones, not being so for various reasons, and that projects such as these help to improve food systems so that food reaches consumers with the required quality and delivers the intended nutrition for human health.

The Principal Agriculture Officer from the Ministry of Agriculture, Margaret Natai, who represented the national food systems Coordinator, said that as a ministry they are collaborating with other stakeholders in order to implement strategies to ensure that sustainable food systems in the country are put into effect.

She said that in 2021 they drew up goals in various sectors and they have guidelines that direct them, including looking at food safety, school feeding for children, food loss and processing.

"Because of that, every stakeholder here has a role to play, and in today's session we are educating stakeholders so that they understand how to organise themselves to reach the goals, including how to use innovative technology in production," said that Officer.

The Director of the Livestock Development Department from the Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation, Natural Resources and Livestock of Zanzibar, Asha Zahran Mohamed, said the workshop will help them to provide education to citizens on improving food systems and the production of meat and milk.

a7318.t:
The First Lady of Nigeria, Oluremi Tinubu, has expressed confidence in the country’s ability to eliminate tuberculosis (TB) by 2035. She highlighted the critical role of partnerships and innovative strategies in overcoming the disease’s impact.
Speaking at the 2024 National TB Conference in Abuja, themed “Public-Private Partnership and Integrated Service Delivery: Panacea to End TB in Nigeria,” the First Lady commended stakeholders for their dedication but stressed the need for sustained efforts to meet global TB elimination targets.
“Despite progress, Nigeria still has the highest TB burden in Africa and ranks sixth globally. The 2024 WHO Global Tuberculosis Report reveals that Nigeria recorded approximately 467,000 TB cases in 2023, underscoring the urgent need for collective action,” she stated.
Oluremi Tinubu acknowledged strides made in diagnosing and treating TB, attributing them to the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda under President Bola Tinubu, along with support from civil society organizations and international partners such as USAID and the Global Fund.
“The solution lies in the strength of partnerships between public and private sectors, alongside integrated service delivery that ensures no one is left behind,” she emphasized.
The First Lady reaffirmed her dedication to eradicating TB, sharing that her previous donation had been used to acquire diagnostic tools, enhance case detection, and improve other vital services.
She praised the conference as a vital platform for exchanging knowledge, developing strategies, and renewing the commitment to combating TB.
As Nigeria continues its fight against tuberculosis, Oluremi Tinubu’s optimism highlights the importance of collaboration, innovation, and unwavering dedication. With sustained effort, the country aims to achieve its goal of eradicating TB by 2035, offering hope for a healthier future for all Nigerians.

a7357.t:
Namibia is still among the countries that are committed to ending AIDS by 2030.
This ambitious goal is being strengthened at a two-day workshop focused on the Sustainability Roadmap and the National Operational Plan, which will outline a comprehensive pathway towards sustained epidemic control of HIV, TB, malaria, and hepatitis.
The Executive Director of the Ministry of Health and Social Services, Ben Nangombe, reiterated that Namibia has made commendable progress in curbing the spread of infectious diseases like HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria.
"We have witnessed significant forward movement in achieving the goals articulated in the National Strategic Framework, thanks in large part to the invaluable support by our Development Cooperation Partners and the active role of Civil Society Organisations (CSOs). The data and figures towards Namibia's achievements of the UNAIDS 95-95-95 fast-tracked targets for HIV are well known to all of you. As of 2022 in Namibia, 94% of HIV-positive individuals know their status, 97% of them are on antiretroviral therapy (ART), and 93% have reached viral suppression (94-97-93)."
The National Operational Plan and Sustainability Roadmap are seen as critical in the final push to eradicate AIDS and other diseases as public health threats by 2030.
The Sustainability Roadmap and National Operational Plan will be launched during this year's World AIDS Day commemoration on the 1st of December.
"This is the last mile, and we dare not relent. We will not falter. Not now, when we have achieved so much. Let us maintain the momentum and deliver a solid NOP and a comprehensive sustainability framework to operationalise our NSF for HIV, TB, malaria, and hepatitis."
PEPFAR Representative Cheryl Amoroso discussed the funding perspective of PEPFAR as a donor.
"From a PEPFAR perspective, we need to already embrace change to together understand the transformation of HIV programming in line with this developing vision that the country has for its future health system, not just from an HIV perspective but holistically. From a donor viewpoint, we are ready to adapt our investments to help realise this developing vision, which is why today and tomorrow are so important. We will use this roadmap to guide our investment. The Namibia PEPFAR investments have already started making shifts better aligned with the future vision that is already developing, and the clarity that we will have on this documentation will continue to support that transition."

اجتمع أمين عام الرئاسة،السيد/ نجيب عبد الله كامل، يوم الأربعاء الماضي،بمثلي الوكالات الدولية والأممية العاملة في جيبوتي، إلى جانب كوادر رفيعة المستوى من وزارة الاقتصاد والمالية المكلفة بالصناعة، ووزارة الميزانية.
وشارك في الاجتماع المنعقد في قاعة المؤتمرات بقصر الشعب، المنسق الوطني لوكالات الأمم المتحدة المقيم في جيبوتي، السيد/ خوسيه باراهونا، إلى جانب ممثلي كل من برنامج الأمم المتحدة الإنمائي، ومنظمة الأمم المتحدة للأغذية والزراعة، والوكالة الأمريكية للتنمية الدولية(USAID)، والوكالة اليابانية للتعاون الدولي(JICA)، ووفد الاتحاد الأوروبي، فضلا عن مدير ديوان رئيس الوزراء، ومدير التمويل الخارجي.
وتمثل الهدف الرئيسي لهذا الاجتماع،في تسليط الضوء على وضع المساعدات التنموية الممنوحة لجيبوتي والحاجة إلى مستوى من النزاهة والحكم الرشيد، وكذلك تعزيز تنسيق الإجراءات والمشاريع قيد التنفيذ».
وألقى السيد/ نجيب عبدَ الله كامل خطابا مقتضباً في الجلسة الافتتاحية للاجتماع، أكد فيها تصميم بلادنا على تعزيز التآزر بين مختلف أصحاب المصلحة، وتعزيز التعاون وتجنب ازدواجية المشاريع،ما من شأنه تحسين تأثير جهودنا الجماعية لجعل آلية المراقبة لدينا أكثر كفاءة، ملفتا الي أن هذا اللقاء يشكِّل فرصة لمناقشة التحديات والفرص والمسائل المتعلقة بالمشاريع ذات الأولوية وفعالية التنسيق».
من الجدير بالذكر الإشارة الي ان مبادرة الأمين العام التي حظيت بالترحيب بالإجماع، تتطلب المزيد من الاجتماعات الدورية من أجل الامتثال للأولويات الأساسية في إقامة أوجه التآزر، والتي تضع في صميم التنسيق والوضوح الكامل ورؤية جميع الشراكات..
تجدر الإشارة إلى أن المناقشات التي عقدها أمين عام رئاسة الوزراء مع الشركاء - خلال هذا الاجتماع- تعزز آلية تقييم لتنشيط الشراكات من خلال تنفيذ برنامج E-Delta، وهو حل وأداة لجمع البيانات لكل ركيزة من ركائز خطة التنمية الوطنية،من أجل توفير الوضوح مما يسمح لبلدنا بالحصول على نظرة عامة شاملة للموارد التي يتلقاها الشركاء، كما ستقوم هذه المنصة بتدريب المستخدمين ونقاط الاتصال في الوزارات القطاعية.
يشار أيضا إلى أن وكالات الأمم المتحدة تضطلع بدور حيويٍّ في تعزيز التنمية المستدامة في البلد، من خلال تقديم المساعدة الفنية والمالية، وتعزيز الصحة والتعليم، وتعزيز الزراعة والأمن الغذائي، وكذلك حماية البيئة والموارد الطبيعية والنهوض بحقوق الإنسان والمساواة.

The Secretary General of the Presidency, Mr Najib Abdallah Kamil, met last Wednesday with representatives of the international and United Nations agencies operating in Djibouti, together with high-level officials from the Ministry of Economy and Finance in charge of Industry, and the Ministry of the Budget.

Taking part in the meeting, held in the conference hall of the People’s Palace, were the Resident National Coordinator of the United Nations agencies in Djibouti, Mr José Barahona, along with representatives of the United Nations Development Programme, the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), and the European Union delegation, as well as the Director of the Prime Minister’s Cabinet and the Director of External Financing.

The main objective of this meeting was to shed light on the state of development assistance granted to Djibouti and the need for a level of integrity and good governance, as well as to strengthen the coordination of ongoing actions and projects.

Mr Najib Abdallah Kamil delivered a brief speech at the opening session of the meeting, in which he affirmed our country’s determination to strengthen synergy among the various stakeholders, and to enhance cooperation and avoid duplication of projects, which would improve the impact of our collective efforts and make our monitoring mechanism more efficient, noting that this meeting constitutes an opportunity to discuss the challenges, opportunities and issues relating to priority projects and to the effectiveness of coordination.

It is worth noting that the Secretary General’s initiative, which was welcomed unanimously, requires more periodic meetings in order to comply with the fundamental priorities in establishing synergies, which place at the heart of coordination full clarity and visibility of all partnerships.

It should be noted that the discussions held by the Secretary General of the Prime Minister’s Office with the partners during this meeting strengthen an evaluation mechanism for revitalising partnerships through the implementation of the E-Delta programme, a solution and data-collection tool for each pillar of the National Development Plan, in order to provide clarity allowing our country to obtain a comprehensive overview of the resources it receives from partners; this platform will also train users and focal points in the sectoral ministries.

It is also noted that the United Nations agencies play a vital role in promoting sustainable development in the country, by providing technical and financial assistance, strengthening health and education, promoting agriculture and food security, as well as protecting the environment and natural resources and advancing human rights and equality.

Commentaries | Aug 16,2025
Federal officials have unveiled a three-pronged allocation strategy for this year’s anticipated avocado bonanza. Of the record 18.1 million tonnes forecasted, half is earmarked for export, 40pc for domestic consumption, and the balance for industrial processing. The government's ambitious vision stakes the country’s hopes on a fruit that accounted for less than a tonne of exports last year, revealing a deep disconnect between aspiration and infrastructure.
At face value, the sheer scale of the leap — from 781Qtls exported last year to a 10,000Qtls target this season — is unprecedented. Yet, this optimism belies logistical bottlenecks, capacity constraints, and structural inefficiencies that plague the nascent avocado value chain.
“We've plans to export most of the avocado harvest,” said Mohammedsani Amin, deputy head of the Oromia Bureau of Agriculture. “Production is scaling up as we collect avocados from smallholder farmers organised in clusters.”
Yet, hard data remain scarce. A Ministry survey pegs domestic demand at roughly 80,000tns a year, a reminder that market knowledge is thin.
The year's export targets are more than a dozen times last year’s shipments. However, variety remains a problem.
“We currently export only one of the seven varieties we grow,” Mohammedsani said, noting that foreign buyers want fruit that most growers do not yet produce in quantity.
Since 2005, the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and Israel’s MASHAV have worked with the Ministry of Agriculture to spread the Hass variety, favoured worldwide for its creamy flesh and thick skin. The program has reached about 2,600 farmers over the past four years and plans to help them export 100tns of Hass this September. It has rolled out modern nurseries and handed out improved seedlings, encouraging early results.
For researchers such as Abayneh Melkie of Debre Markos University, the weak link is post-harvest handling.
“Farmers don't know how to handle avocados after harvest,” he said. “This contributes to quality loss.”
He urged government-led awareness drives, more investment in refrigerated transport, expanded cultivation of export-friendly varieties and better packaging.
Officials are carving out cultivation clusters of 200hct to 300hct. On one 172hct block in the Ada’a and Lume districts southeast of Addis Abeba, in Oromia Regional State, 1,088 smallholders were tending trees supplied by public nurseries. The seedlings are free, and the farmers received subsidised soil and water tests. Those who want extra saplings can buy them for 50 Br to 120 Br from donor projects or private nurseries prized for reliable quality.
Farmers already feel the problem.
“Seedlings are expensive, and the current varieties need heavy watering and compost,” said Mengistu Tesfaye, manager of the Southern Ethiopia's Kayu Fruits & Vegetables Cooperative Union. “We also don’t have enough variety to meet market needs.”
According to Mengistu, intermediaries often dump ripe and unripe fruit together in flimsy sacks, bruising the crop.
“It ruins the fruit and sometimes damages future harvests,” he told Fortune.
Transport is another headache. Avocados travel best in cold trucks, but refrigerated vehicles are scarce. Even so, Mengistu said the Union has sold 55,000Kg this year, including 33,000Kg to a company operating in one of the industrial parks, and hopes to hit 70,000Kg by December. National shipments remain small but are inching up.
“Our exports have grown from eight to 14tns in two years,” said Wale Getaneh, project coordinator at the Ethiopian Horticulture Producer Exporters Association.
Prices rose to 5.7 dollars a kilogram from 3.6 dollars. An eight-tonne sea consignment recently left for Rotterdam, the Netherlands, to test the waters. The trip took 36 days, slowed by delays in securing refrigerated containers, but the reception in Europe was positive.
“I advise the private sector to invest in avocado exports,” Wale said. “The government should offer incentives to make this sector attractive.”
Nonetheless, exporters with more than hope have found the path rocky.
Rahewa Mohammed, who has been in the trade for three years, sources most of her fruit from Mizan Teferi in the South West Regional State and Addis Abeba, shipping mainly to Dubai and other Middle East markets. She is active nine months of the year; February, March, and April bring no crop.
“Payment issues and amendments are my biggest challenges,” she told Fortune. “Sometimes, I ship 4,000Kg but receive less than that. I don't find out until it arrives."
It takes months for her to settle the difference. Documents travel with the fruit; she risks losing her investment if anything goes wrong. At times, she said, she is not paid at all.
Elias Gulilat left the business after a year. His Turkish buyer came to Ethiopia but left empty-handed because he did not get the variety he wanted.
“Even worse, we shipped to people who disappeared after receiving our produce,” he said.
Finding rogue buyers can be slow, even when organisations such as the Addis Abeba Chamber of Commerce & Sectoral Associations intervene. According to Zekarias Assefa, the deputy secretary-general, the Chamber steps in by contacting embassies or foreign chambers to track down errant buyers.
Ethiopia’s wager on avocados is bold, and the potential rewards are large. Demand for the fruit has surged worldwide, and the country’s highland soils and mild climate can yield three harvests a year. But bridging the gap between orchard and overseas supermarket will require better roads, cold storage, trustworthy trade partners and the overlooked skill of delivering a ripe avocado without bruises.
Backers of the new strategy say it can work if every link in the chain — from nurseries to shipping lines — tightens up. The government is betting that a humble fruit can mint millions in hard currency and still leave enough on local plates.
